10.26. Subprograms for Dynamic Memory
       Allocation
         The subprograms described in this section provide the capability of dynamically
         allocating and de-allocating storage for a based data-item within a COBOL program.
         UCS COBOL has two separate mechanisms for defining based storage and two kinds
         of pointers. The first method uses the USING POINTER clause on 01 level declarations
         in the WORKING-STORAGE SECTION to define both, a based item and the pointer it is
         based on. Those pointers must be declared as PIC 1(36) BINARY-1, and hold one-word
         VA (Virtual Address) addresses. They have word granularity and can only point at word
         boundaries. You give them a pointer value by calling LOC$ to point it at an existing 01
         or 77 item, by calling UCOBMALLOC$ to allocate new storage, or by doing binary
         arithmetic on them.

         Example:

                 IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
                 PROGRAM-ID. VAexample.
                 DATA DIVISION.
                 WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
                 77 sz PIC S9(10) BINARY.
                 77 stat PIC S9(10) BINARY.
                 77 ptr1 PIC 1(36) BINARY-1.
                 77 ptrcur PIC 1(36) BINARY-1.
                 77 i14   PIC S9(10) BINARY VALUE 14.
                 01 mynames USING POINTER ptr1.
                     03 names PIC X(48) OCCURS 100 TIMES.
                 01 current-name PIC X(48) USING POINTER ptrcur.
                 PROCEDURE DIVISION.
                 ST.
                     MOVE FUNCTION LENGTH(mynames) TO sz.
                     CALL "UCOBMALLOC$" USING sz ptr1 stat.
                     IF stat IS NOT EQUAL TO 0 OR ptr1 IS EQUAL TO 0 STOP RUN.
                     MOVE "John Doe" TO names(i14).
                * Remember, VA pointers can only point to word boundaries:
                     COMPUTE ptrcur = ptr1 + ( 48 / 4 ) * (i14 - 1).
                     IF current-name IS NOT EQUAL TO "John Doe"
                        DISPLAY "*ERROR: " current-name.




7831 0455ΓÇô022                                                                             10ΓÇô77
Using Executive Requests




        The second method is compatible with the IBM COBOL pointer and based storage
        facility. You declare a pointer variable as having USAGE POINTER, and the based
        structure is declared in the LINKAGE SECTION. You SET the ADDRESS OF the based
        structure to either the ADDRESS OF some other structure or variable (at any level) or
        to a pointer that was declared as USAGE POINTER. This newer pointer form has byte
        granularity and can point at byte boundaries, and the UCS C two-word pointer form is
        used for the pointers. (They are compatible with UCS C pointers.) You give a pointer a
        value by calling LOC$ to point it at some other 01 structure, by calling
        UCOBMALLOC$2 to get new storage or by a SET statement. The SET statement can
        set a pointer to the value of another pointer or to the ADDRESS OF some other
        structure or substructure (any level). You cannot do arithmetic on these C-style
        pointers (adding 1 to one of these pointers would NOT cause it to point at the next
        byte).

        Example:

             IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
             PROGRAM-ID. CPTRexample.
             DATA DIVISION.
             WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
             77 sz PIC S9(10) BINARY.
             77 stat PIC S9(10) BINARY.
             77 newptr USAGE POINTER.
             77 i14   PIC S9(10) BINARY VALUE 14.
             LINKAGE SECTION.
             01 mynames.
                 03 names PIC X(48) OCCURS 100 TIMES.
             01 current-name PIC X(48).
             PROCEDURE DIVISION.
             ST.
                 MOVE FUNCTION LENGTH(mynames) TO sz.
                 CALL "UCOBMALLOC$2" USING sz newptr stat.
                 IF stat IS NOT EQUAL 0 OR newptr is EQUAL TO NULL STOP RUN.
                 SET ADDRESS OF mynames TO newptr.
                 MOVE "John Doe" TO names(i14).
                 SET ADDRESS OF current-name TO ADDRESS OF names(i14).
                 IF current-name IS NOT EQUAL TO "John Doe"
                    DISPLAY "*ERROR: '" current-name "'".

        See the UCS COBOL Programming Reference Manual Volume 1, COBOL Statements,
        for more information on using the USING POINTER clause and the USAGE POINTER
        clause.

        The memory allocation routines call the URTS runtime system to find space in data
        banks for the memory requests. The OS 2200 M-Series architecture supports the
        following databank types:

        ∩é╖   Small banks (218 words = 262,144 words)
        ∩é╖   Large banks (224 words = 16,777,216 words)
        ∩é╖   Very large banks (230 = 1,073,741,824 words)



10ΓÇô78                                                                           7831 0455ΓÇô022
                                                                     Using Executive Requests




         Note: The M-Series architecture supports very large banks, up to 233 words in size.
         However, the Operating System currently only supports very large banks up to 230
         words in size. A very large bank (VLB) is made up of consecutive smaller banks. The
         system imposes limits on the number of banks according to the address tree level.
         See the Linking System Programming Reference Manual for documented limits. For a
         given program, the Exec and the Linking System might allocate a few additional
         banks at each address level for internal use. The actual number of banks allocated
         for internal use can vary. Consequently, the maximum size of a very large bank is
         smaller than the limits specified.

         The UCS COBOL compiler allocates automatic variables in a small bank (the ALS)
         and allocates static variables in a small or large bank depending on the size of the
         static data items. (In UCOB generated-code, WORKING-STORAGE local variables are
         put into automatic storage when the INITIAL clause is used on the PROGRAM-ID
         statement.) The memory allocation subprograms add the capability of creating a VLB
         through this allocation process. However, generated code from the UCS compilers
         (UCOB, UC, UFTN, UPLS) cannot easily reference data beyond the first 224 words in
         a VLB, so use of VLBs is discouraged. No single data structure or array must exceed
         224 words in size. Blobs are an exception as they are handled as a unit.

         There are two sets of memory allocation subprograms; one set working with
         one-word VA pointers and one set working with 2-word C-style pointers. The
         interfaces are identical with the exception of the pointer form. When an allocation call
         succeeds, the returned pointer can be used to access a based object in the space
         allocated until the space is explicitly freed or reallocated. Allocation fails if storage is
         not available to satisfy the request. You must check the value of the returned pointer.
         A zero or NULL pointer value indicates failure. A return status parameter will also be
         non-zero on a failure and provides additional information.

         The memory allocation subprograms that work with the one-word VA pointers are:

         ∩é╖   UCOBMALLOC$
         ∩é╖   UCOBCALLOC$
         ∩é╖   UCOBFREE$
         ∩é╖   UCOBREALLOC$

         The memory allocation subprograms that work with the two-word C-style pointers
         are:

         ∩é╖   UCOBMALLOC$2
         ∩é╖   UCOBCALLOC$2
         ∩é╖   UCOBFREE$2
         ∩é╖   UCOBREALLOC$2




7831 0455ΓÇô022                                                                                  10ΓÇô79
Using Executive Requests




10.26.1. UCOBMALLOC$
        Function
        The UCOBMALLOC$ subprogram allocates storage for the number of bytes specified
        by number-of-bytes, returns the address (VA) of the storage allocated in
        address-name, and the return status of the operation in return-status.

        Format
          CALL 'UCOBMALLOC$' USING number-of-bytes, address-name, return-status

        where:

        number-of-bytes

           is an integer variable. Define number-of-bytes as PIC 1(36) BINARY-1.

        address-name

           is an integer variable. Define address-name as PIC 1(36) BINARY-1.

        return-status

           is an integer variable. Define return-status as PIC 1(36) BINARY-1. See Table 10ΓÇô12
           for possible values.

10.26.2. UCOBCALLOC$
        Function
        The UCOBCALLOC$ subprogram allocates storage for the number of bytes specified
        by number-of-bytes, clears the allocated area to binary zero, returns the address of
        the storage allocated in address-name, and the return status of the operation in
        return-status.

        Format
          CALL 'UCOBCALLOC$' USING number-of-bytes, address-name, return-status

        where:

        number-of-bytes

           is an integer variable. Define number-of-bytes as PIC 1(36) BINARY-1.

        address-name

           is an integer variable. Define address-name as PIC 1(36) BINARY-1.




10ΓÇô80                                                                           7831 0455ΓÇô022
                                                                 Using Executive Requests




         return-status

            is an integer variable. Define return-status as PIC 1(36) BINARY-1. See Table 10ΓÇô12
            for possible values.

10.26.3. UCOBFREE$
         Function
         The UCOBFREE$ subprogram de-allocates the storage at the address contained in
         address-name and the return status of the operation in return-status. The address in
         address-name must refer to the address returned from a call to UCOBMALLOC$,
         UCOBCALLOC$, or UCOBREALLOC$.

         Format
           CALL 'UCOBFREE$' USING address-name, return-status

         where:

         address-name

            is an integer variable. Define address-name as PIC 1(36) BINARY-1.

         return-status

            is an integer variable. Define return-status as PIC 1(36) BINARY-1. See Table 10ΓÇô12
            for possible values.

10.26.4. UCOBREALLOC$
         Function
         The UCOBREALLOC$ subprogram attempts to allocate storage within the storage
         pointed to by address-name-1. The contents of the address-name-1 is set by a prior
         call to UCOBMALLOC$, UCOBREALLOC$, or UCOBCALLOC$. If the size of the storage
         previously allocated is equal or greater than the contents of number-of-bytes, the
         previously allocated storage is reused and the address of the storage is placed in
         address-name-2. If the size of the previously allocated storage is less than the
         contents of number-of-bytes, new storage is allocated and the address is placed in
         address-name-2. The number-of-bytes bytes of storage from the previous allocation
         is also moved to the new allocation and the previous storage is freed. The return
         status of the operation is placed in return-status.

         Format
           CALL 'UCOBREALLOC$' USING address-name-1, number-of-bytes, address-
           name-2,
           return-status




7831 0455ΓÇô022                                                                             10ΓÇô81
Using Executive Requests




        where:

        address-name-1

           is an integer variable. Define address-name-1 as PIC 1(36) BINARY-1.

        number-of-bytes

           is an integer variable. Define number-of-bytes as PIC 1(36) BINARY-1.

        address-name-2

           is an integer variable. Define address-name-2 as PIC 1(36) BINARY-1.

        return-status

           is an integer variable. Define return-status as PIC 1(36) BINARY-1. See Table 10ΓÇô12
           for possible values.

        return-status

10.27. Interface to Zip Utilities
         COBOL users now have the ability to access data from a zip file on the OS 2200. In
         addition, they can compress data on the OS 2200 into a zip file. This interface requires
         the use of CIFS for ClearPath OS 2200 (see the CIFS for ClearPath OS 2200 User,
         Programmer, and Administrator Reference Manual). This interface allows COBOL
         applications to read data directly from the compressed zip file, as needed. In addition,
         this capability allows the COBOL user to take data from the OS 2200, compress it, and
         write it to a zip file.

         This feature uses interfaces to the ZIPUT Processor that is a component of CIFS to
         compress and decompress the data.

         In order to accomplish the desired task of reading/writing compressed data from a zip
         file; the COBOL user must have the following capabilities:

         ∩é╖   The ability to determine the number of entries in a specified zip file.
         ∩é╖   The ability to determine the names of each of the entries in a zip file.
         ∩é╖   The ability to read data from a specified entry in a zip file.
         ∩é╖   The ability to write data to a specified entry in a zip file.
         ∩é╖   The ability to close a zip file once all the data has been written to it.
         ∩é╖   The ability to set the compression level for subsequent zip file entries.

         The user must also be able to determine if an error occurred during the processing of
         the data so that the appropriate action can be taken.

         Parameters containing an error status, size, or number must start on a word boundary.
         These are 01/77 level variables declared, for example, as PIC 9 (10) BINARY, PIC S9 (10)
         BINARY.

         The subsections that follow describe the COBOL callable entries that can be used to
         access zip files from the 2200.

10.27.1. ZIP$NBRENTRIES
         Function
         This routine is called to determine the number of entries that are contained in a
         specified zip file.




7831 0455ΓÇô022                                                                                10ΓÇô85
Using Executive Requests




        Format
          CALL 'ZIP$NBRENTRIES'         USING zipfile-name, nbr-of-entries, error-
          status.

        where:

        zipfile-name

            is a variable that contains the name of the zip file that is to be checked. This field is
            described as PIC X(n) and must be followed by a null character (low-values).

        nbr-of-entries

            is a variable into which the number of entries that the zip file contains will be
            returned. This variable must be defined as PIC 9(10) BINARY.

        error-status

            is a variable into which the status of the operation is returned. This variable must
            be defined as PIC 9(10) BINARY.

        The error statuses returned by this routine are as follows:

           0        Normal return
           1        Invalid name specified for the zip file
           2        Zip file could not be found or in error
           3        File name or entry could not be found
           6        Out of memory
           9        Internal error during initialization of the URTS zip utilities

        Example
          01     zipgrp.
                 02 zipfile-name pic x(20) value 'test.zip'.
                 02 nulterm pic x value low-values.
          01     nbr-of-entries pic 9(10) binary value 0.
          01     error-status pic 9(10) binary value 0.

               CALL 'ZIP$NBRENTRIES'
                    USING zipfile-name nbr-of-entries error-status.

                                                                     Using Executive Requests




10.27.2. ZIP$NAMEENTRIES
         Function
         This routine is called to retrieve the name of each of the entries in a specified zip file.
         It will also return the number of entries in the zip file.

         The name of each entry is placed into the buffer that was passed to this routine. The
         size allowed for each name is also passed to this routine. If the name is smaller than
         the buffer being filled in, it is space padded. If the name is larger than the buffer that is
         being filled in, the name is truncated and an error status is returned.

         Format
           CALL 'ZIP$NAMEENTRIES' USING
                zipfile-name, buffer-for-names nbr-of-entries, entry-size, error-
           status.

         where:

         zipfile-name

             is a variable that contains the name of the zip file that is to be checked. This field is
             described as PIC X(n) and must be followed by a null character (low-values).

         buffer-for-names

             is the buffer into which entry names in the specified zip file will be placed.

         nbr-of-entries

             is a variable into which the number of entries that the zip file contains will be
             returned. This variable must be defined as PIC 9(10) BINARY.

         entry-size

             is a variable that contains the size of buffer into which the entry name will be
             stored. This variable must be defined as PIC 9(10) BINARY.

         error-status

         is a variable into which the status of the operation is returned. This variable must be
         defined as PIC 9(10) BINARY.

         The error statuses returned by this routine are as follows:

                  0       Normal return
                  1       Invalid name specified for the zip file
                  2       Zip file could not be found or in error
                  3       Zip file not found
                  4       Entry name was truncated



7831 0455ΓÇô022                                                                                    10ΓÇô87
Using Executive Requests




                 5      Unexpected exception
                 6      Out of memory
                 9      Internal error during initialization of the URTS zip utilities

        Example
          01     zipgrp.
                 02 zipfile-name pic x(20) value 'test8.zip'.
                 02 nulterm pic x value low-values.
          01     nbr-of-entries pic 9(10) binary.
          01     entry-size pic 9(10) binary value 25.
          01     buffer-for-names.
                 02 name-of-entry pic x(25) occurs 30 times value space.
          01     error-status pic 9(10) binary.

              CALL 'ZIP$NAMEENTRIES'
                    USING zipfile-name buffer-for-names nbr-of-entries entry-size
          error-status.

10.27.4. ZIP$WRITEENTRY
        Function
        This routine is called to write a buffer of data to an entry in a zip file. The utility will
        compress the data and write it to the appropriate zip file entry. If an error is detected,
        the appropriate error status is returned from this routine. The default compression
        level will be used unless the ZIP$SETCOMPRESSION utility has been called. See
        10.27.7 for additional information on ZIP$SETCOMPRESSION.

        Format
          CALL 'ZIP$WRITEENTRY' USING
               zipfile-name, entry-name, buffer, buffer-size, error-status.

        where:

        zipfile-name

            is a variable that contains the name of the zip file that is to be checked. This field is
            described as PIC X(n) and must be followed by a null character (low-values).

        entry-name

            is a variable that contains the name of the entry within the zip file that is to be
            written. This variable is describes as PIC X(n).

        buffer

            is the buffer that contains the data that is to be written to the zip file entry.

        buffer-size

            is a variable that contains the number of characters that are in buffer. This variable
            must be defined as PIC 9(10) BINARY.

        error-status

            is a variable into which the status of the operation is returned. This variable must
            be defined as PIC 9(10) BINARY.

        The error statuses returned by this routine are as follows:

            0    Normal return
            1    Zip file name could not be converted to string
            2    Zip file could not be found or in error
            3    Attempt to write a buffer to an entry that has already been
                 written to and is closed.
            4    Zip file name or entry name are all spaces
            5    Size of buffer to be written is less than or equal to 0.
            6    Out of memory



10ΓÇô90                                                                                7831 0455ΓÇô022
                                                                          Using Executive Requests




               7    Unexpected exception
               9    Internal error during initialization of the URTS zip utilities

         Example
           01       zipgrp.
                    02 zipfile-name pic x(20) value 'ziptest15.zip'.
                    02 nulterm pic x value low-values.
           01       error-status pic 9(10) binary value 0.
           01       buffer pic x(50) value all 'a'.
           01       entry-name-group.
                    02 entry-name pic x(25).
           01       buffer-size pic 9(10) binary.

                     CALL 'ZIP$WRITEENTRY'
                       USING zipgrp entry-name-group, buffer,buffer-size, error-status.


10.27.5. ZIP$CLOSEENTRY
         Function
         This routine is called from the COBOL program in order to close the zip file that is
         being written to. This routine need only be called following the completion of the
         ZIP$WRITEENTRY routine in order for the last buffer to be written out.

         Format
           CALL 'ZIP$CLOSEENTRY' USING error-status.

         where error-status is a variable into which the status of the operation is returned. This
         variable must be defined as PIC 9(10) BINARY.

         The possible error statuses that are returned are as follows:

           0       Normal return
           2       Zip file could not be found or in error
           3       Attempt to close zip file without ever writing to one
           6       Out of memory
           9       Internal error during initialization of the URTS zip utilities

         Example
           01       error-status pic 9(10) binary value 0.

                   CALL 'ZIP$CLOSEENTRY' USING error-status.

10.27.6. ZIP$PRINTEXCEPTION
          Function
          This routine is called to print the error exception that occurred during the processing
          of a zip file. This utility should be called if a nonzero error status was returned from
          one of the other zip utilities. This routine will then print the message that is associated
          with the error status.

          Format
             CALL 'ZIP$PRINTEXCEPTION' USING error-status.

          where error-status is the variable into which the status of the operation is returned.
          This variable must be defined as pic 9(10) binary.

          The possible error statuses returned by this routine are as follows:

             0     Normal return
             1     No exception to print
             9     Internal error during initialization of the URTS zip utilities

          Example
             01     error-status pic 9(10) binary value 0.
                  CALL 'ZIP$PRINTEXCEPTION' USING error-status.


10.27.7. ZIP$SETCOMPRESSION
          Function
          This routine is called to set the compression level of subsequent zip file entries. The
          new compression level will not take effect until the first write to a new zip file entry.
          The new compression level will stay in effect until ZIP$SETCOMPRESSION is called
          again. Valid compression levels are -1 to 9 (-1 is the default, 0 is no compression, 1 is
          best speed, 9 is best compression).

          Format
                  CALL 'ZIP$SETCOMPRESSION' USING compression-level error-status.

        where:

        compression-level

                 is a variable that contains the compression level to be used on subsequent zip file
                 entries. This variable must be defined as pic s9(10) binary.

        error-status

                 is the variable into which the status of the operation is returned. This variable must
                 be defined as pic 9(10) binary.




10ΓÇô92                                                                                  7831 0455ΓÇô022
                                                                         Using Executive Requests




          The error statuses returned by this routine are as follows:

            0     Normal return
            1     Compressed level is invalid
            2     Error occurred during setting of the compression level
            9     Internal error during initialization of the URTS zip utilities
Example
                01   compression-level pic s9(10) binary.
                01   error-status pic 9(10) binary value 0.

                     MOVE 4 TO compression-level.
                     CALL 'ZIP$SETCOMPRESSION'
                           USING compression-level error-status.

10.28. Retrieving Coordinated Universal Time (UTC)
         COBOL users now have the ability to retrieve the Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).
         This feature is available only if the machine architecture supports UTC.

         This feature provides user interfaces to retrieve UTC time as well as the information
         necessary to determine the local time equivalent. The feature uses the Exec interface
         SYSTEM$TIME. For complete details on this interface, see the System Services
         Programming Reference Manual.

         The subsections that follow describe the COBOL callable routines that can be used to
         access UTC time.

         Note: If you use the UTC time functions in HVTIP, you must use the INITIAL clause
         on the PROGRAM-ID.

10.28.1. UTC$TIME
         Function
         This routine is called to return the UTC time in UCSDWTIME$ format. The routine
         UCSCNVTIM$CC can then be used to convert the UTC time into a character format.

         Format
           CALL 'UTC$TIME'       USING parm, returnstatus.

         where:

         parm

         is a structure that will contain the result of the routine. It should be in the following
         format:

           01     parm.
                  02 version pic 9(5) binary value 0.
                  02 filler pic 9(5) binary value 0.
                  02 timeb
                     03 dwtime pic s1(72) binary-1 value 0.

                      03 daylight-savings pic 9(5) binary value 0.
                      03 time-differential pic s9(5) binary value 0.
                      03 time-zone pic xxxx value space.

             where:

             version is the version of the packet being used.




7831 0455ΓÇô022                                                                                   10ΓÇô97
Using Executive Requests




            timeb is the structure that contains the following:

                 dwtime              is the UTC time expressed in UCSDWTIME$ format.
                 daylight-savings    is a flag indicating if daylight saving time is in effect.
                 time-differential   contains the differential between UTC and local time.
                 time-zone           is the mnemonic for the local time zone.

        returnstatus

        is a variable into which the status of the operation is returned. The status is returned
        in ELMS format and must be defined as follows:

          01   returnstatus.
               02 elms.
                   03 prod-id    pic 1(18) binary-1.
                   03 res        pic 1(3) binary-1.
                   03 message-id pic 1(15) binary-1.
               02 aux     pic s9(10) binary.

        The message-id variable can be examined to determine the status of the call. The
        following values can be returned:

                 0        is the UTC time expressed in UCSDWTIME$ format.
                 96       system configuration does not allow for UTC time.

            Refer to the System Services Programming Reference Manual for all other values
            returned.

        See 10.28.3 for an example of using the UTC$TIME routine.

10.28.2. TIMEB2DWTIM$
        Function
        This routine is called to convert the UTC time returned by UTC$TIME to local time. The
        time differential and daylight saving time flag will be used in doing the conversion. The
        local time will be returned in UCSDWTIME$ format.

        The routine UCSCNVTIM$CC can then be used to convert the local time into a
        character format.




10ΓÇô98                                                                                7831 0455ΓÇô022
                                                                 Using Executive Requests




         Format
           CALL 'TIMEB2DWTIM$' USING timeb, localtime.

         where:

         timeb

            is a variable that contains the UTC time returned by the UTC$TIME routine that
            needs to be converted to local time. This time is in UCSDWTIME$ format. See
            10.28.1 for information on how to obtain this variable.

         localtime

            is a variable that will contain the local time that was derived from the UTC time.
            This local time will be in UCSDWTIME$ format. This variable should be defined as
            pic s1(72) binary-1.

         See 10.28.3 for an example of using the TIMEB2DWTIM$ routine.

Section 11
Transaction Processing in UCS

         Programs written in COBOL, FORTRAN, and C can be executed in a Transaction
         Processing (TIP) or High-Volume Transaction Processing (HVTIP or HVTIP2)
         environment within the Universal Compiling System (UCS). Table 11ΓÇô1 shows the
         transaction processing interfaces supported for these three host languages.


            Table 11ΓÇô1. Transaction Processing Interfaces from UCS Languages


                   UCS COBOL                      UCS FORTRAN                       UCS C

          DPS 2200                        DPS 2200                      DPS 2200
          MCB                             MCB                           MCB
          Primitives that do not handle   Primitives that do not handle Primitives that do not handle
          messages                        messages                      messages
          DMS 2200                        DMS 2200
          RDMS 2200 SQL Embedded          RDMS 2200 SQL                 RDMS 2200 SQL
          SQL
          SFS 2200 Relative access        SFS 2200 Direct access        SFS 2200 Binary access (direct
          (direct SDF) Indexed access     (direct SDF)                  SDF)
          (MSAM)
          PCIOS                           PCIOS                         PCIOS
          FCSS                            FCSS                          FCSS


         Notice that Message Control Bank (MCB) and Display Processing System (DPS 2200)
         functions are supported for all three host languages. Most primitives that do not
         handle messages are supported by the UCS host languages. COMPOOL
         message-buffering primitives, however, are not supported in UCS programming for
         any language.

         All three host languages can access the Universal Data System (UDS) relational
         database model (RDMS 2200) and the conventional Shared File System (SFS 2200). The
         network-hierarchical Database Management System (DMS 2200) is supported only for
         UCS COBOL and UCS FORTRAN.

         UCS COBOL includes an embedded SQL interface for RDMS 2200.




7831 0455ΓÇô022                                                                                       11ΓÇô1
Transaction Processing in UCS




        A production TIP transaction that wishes to have TIP sticking and RESTART should not
        have PADS as its contingency routine. PADS does a CREATE$BANK call to the Exec
        and this kills TIP sticking and RESTART for the transaction. One way to keep PADS out
        is to name the URTS runtime library in the RESOLVE statement in the static link of your
        transaction. This results in PADS stub object module C$NPADS being linked into your
        program.

            RESOLVE ALL REFERENCES USING L_D,SYS$LIB$*EMOMRTS.,LCN

        Another way is to specifically include the C$NPADS object module from the URTS
        library along with using the LOCAL_DEFS (or L_D) option in the RESOLVE statement in
        your static link:

            INCLUDE SYS$LIB$*EMOMRTS.C$NPADS
            RESOLVE ALL REFERENCES USING L_D,LCN

        For a more detailed description of transaction processing, see the following
        documents:

        ∩é╖    Application Development Solutions Application Development Programming
             Guide (7831 4077)
        ∩é╖    Configuration and Operations Guide (7833 1550)
        ∩é╖    ClearPath OS 2200 Display Processing System (DPS 2200) Run-Time
             Programming Reference Manual (7830 7840)
        ∩é╖    Transaction Processing Applications Programming Guide (7830 9986)


11.1. Using DPS 2200 Functions to Code
      Transactions
        DPS 2200 supports transactions written in UCS COBOL. DPS 2200 provides a simple
        call interface to perform its work, as shown in the following skeleton:

            CALL 'D$INIT' USING DPS-STATUS, INFO-BUFFER.
              .
              .
              .
            CALL 'D$OPEN' USING DPS-STATUS, SCREEN-xxxxx-nn.
              .
              .
              .
            CALL 'D$SEND' USING DPS-STATUS, SCREEN-xxxxx-nn.
              .
              .
              .

        The statements used to call DPS 2200 in UCS programs are the same as in non-UCS
        programs. The same DPS 2200 software and forms files can be used in both
        environments simultaneously.




11ΓÇô2                                                                            7831 0455ΓÇô022
                                                               Transaction Processing in UCS




         UCS TIP and HVTIP transactions that access DPS 2200 can use either MCB or
         COMPOOL message buffering, depending on the following conditions:

         ∩é╖    VALTAB STATUS keyword setting
         ∩é╖    Availability of the MCB software
         ∩é╖    The designation of MCB message buffering in the SILAS configuration

         MCB message buffering is used if the following conditions exist:

         ∩é╖    STA,J is specified in the VALTAB entry.
         ∩é╖    MCB software is available.
         ∩é╖    MCB message buffering is designated in SILAS.

         If the STA keyword is specified without J, then COMPOOL message buffering is used.


11.2. Using MCB Functions to Code Transactions
         All UCS TIP and HVTIP transactions can directly call MCB functions. The host language
         UCS COBOL supports calls to MCB functions, using the following generic syntax:

             CALL 'MCB$ENT' USING p-mcb-packet, p-mcb-status
                                  [, msg-buffer[, multi-dest-list]].

         Notice that a call to MCB in a UCS program differs from one in a non-UCS program
         because it includes two additional optional parameters, as follows:
         msg-buffer

              The parameter for the message buffer identifies the storage area into which
              messages are read and from which messages are sent by the transaction. This
              parameter eliminates the need for the CLOCTE call used in ASCII COBOL programs
              to set up this buffer address.

         multi-dest-list

              The fourth parameter, multi-dest-list, provides a simple method for identifying a
              multiple-destination list of position identifiers (PID). This parameter eliminates the
              need for the CLOCTE call used in ASCII COBOL programs to set up this buffer
              address.

         Transactions that use MCB functions require the following:

         ∩é╖    Declarations of the MCB functions
         ∩é╖    Allocation of storage space for the MCB packet
         ∩é╖    MCB error message handling buffers
         ∩é╖    In some cases, a message buffer




7831 0455ΓÇô022                                                                                    11ΓÇô3
Transaction Processing in UCS




        To aid the UCS programmer in coding these requirements, the MCB release tape
        includes sample UCS COBOL procedures for these buffers that you can use as a
        template. The element containing these procedures, MCBDEF-UCOB, is found in the
        MCB installation file.


11.3. Using Primitives That Do Not Handle
      Messages to Code Transactions
        UCS programming supports the following primitives that do not handle messages for
        UCS COBOL:

        ∩é╖   COMMIT and ROLLBACK
        ∩é╖   CONECT and DISCON
        ∩é╖   All file-handling functions in the File Control Super Structure (FCSS)
        ∩é╖   TIMER call primitives for scheduling transaction execution at a future time:
            TIMABS, TIMDEL, TIMREL, TIMUPA, and TIMUPR
        ∩é╖   Primitives for the execution-option indicator: UOPAND, UOPGET, and UOPTOR

        The COMPOOL message-handling primitives are not supported in UCS programming.

        The coding of primitives has not changed in UCS programs, except the function
        names, as shown in the following table.


               Previous Name         UCS Name

                  CCONET              CONECT
                  CDISCN              DISCON
                  CCMMIT              COMMIT
                  CRLBAK             ROLLBACK
                   CFCSS                FCSS
                  CUOPND              UOPAND
                  CUOPGT              UOPGET
                  CUOPTR              UOPTOR
                  CTMABS              TIMABS
                  CTMDEL              TIMDEL
                  CTMREL              TIMREL
                  CTMUPA              TIMUPA
                  CTMUPR              TIMUPR


        The previous name of each call is supported in UCS COBOL transactions, but you
        should use the UCS name when coding new UCS transactions or upgrading existing
        transactions to UCS.

11.4. Retrieving the TIP RESTART Status
      (UCOB_RESTARTCHECK and
      UCS_RESTARTCHECK)
         This routine returns a value that indicates whether the current execution is from an
         initial program load or from a TIP RESTART/BT-Load.

         Format
           CALL ΓÇÖUCOB_RESTARTCHECKΓÇÖ USING ret-value.

         where ret-value is a word binary integer that tells you how the currently executing
         program was loaded. The returned values are

           0     is an initial program load
           1     is a TIP RESTART
           2     is an HVTIP RESTART
           3     is a TIP BT-Load


         UCOB_RESTARTCHECK is also available as the parameterless function
         UCS_RESTARTCHECK. Languages that can use functions (such as C and FORTRAN) can
         call this function instead of UCOB_RESTARTCHECK if they wish.

         Description
         A TIP or HVTIP program that has TIP sticking can experience a TIP RESTART. After the
         programΓÇÖs exit, if there is another transaction of the same trancode that is queued or
         that is scheduled within a short time of the exit, the Exec restarts execution of the
         transaction at its starting address. The state of the data banks of the transaction are as
         they were on program exit. In the case of an HVTIP transaction, the HVTIP loader
         reloads data as needed and the rest of the run-time system and user code not need to
         do anything special. If it is a self-initializing (PRGTYP 2) or reentrant (PRGTYP 3) TIP
         transaction, the UCS Runtime System reinitializes its run-time data. However, it is up
         to each individual user program to reinitialize any of its own data that will be needed
         for correct execution.

         A TIP transaction can also be loaded by what is called a BT-Load (Block-Transfer Load).
         The D-banks of the transaction are loaded from another running copy of the
         transaction. BT-Loads can occur if the K and I options are on the STATUS VALTAB
         entry for the transaction and if the BTLOADING flagbox bit is on. However, due to the
         way BT-Loads are done, the data may not be consistent and correct reinitialization
         may be impossible to do. Incorrect program execution can result. For example, if a TIP
         transaction calls an FLSS (Fast-Load Self-Contained Subsystem), BT-Loads must not
         be enabled for the transaction. If your TIP transaction experiences random failures
         when loaded by TIP BT-Loads, then donΓÇÖt use them. TIP/HVTIP RESTARTs are much
         more reliable since data is in a consistent state from a clean program exit.




7831 0455ΓÇô022                                                                                 11ΓÇô5
Transaction Processing in UCS




        The reason for TIP RESTARTs and BT-Loads is performance. When a TIP RESTART or
        BT-Load occurs and the transaction is restarted

        ∩é╖   The Exec does not have to allocate banks and load the transaction.
        ∩é╖   The system does not have to allocate memory pages to the transaction since the
            memory has already been allocated by the previous execution.

        To get TIP sticking and RESTART

        ∩é╖   The program type (PRGTYP) must be self-initializing (2), reentrant (3), or HVTIP (5).
        ∩é╖   The I option must be on the STATUS VALTAB entry.
        ∩é╖   The STICKING flagbox bit must be on.

        A number of factors can inhibit TIP sticking and RESTART:

        ∩é╖   Any contingency
        ∩é╖   Any symbiont prints (DISPLAY statements)
        ∩é╖   Not detaching from MCB
        ∩é╖   Having an active TERMREG at program exit
        ∩é╖   Any create-bank or modify-bank calls to the Exec
        ∩é╖   Not exiting via the normal URTS exit
        ∩é╖   Any files that have been assigned must be freed before program exit

        See ΓÇ£Using Performance Improvement TechniquesΓÇ¥ in the Transaction Processing
        Programming Reference Manual for information on TIP sticking and RESTART. For
        information on VALTAB entries and the VTBUTL utility see ΓÇ£Registering Transaction
        ProgramsΓÇ¥ in the Transaction Processing Administration and Operations Reference
        Manual.

        Example
        IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
        PROGRAM-ID. RESTARTCHECK.
        ENVIRONMENT DIVISION.
        CONFIGURATION SECTION.
        SPECIAL-NAMES.
            PRINTER IS PRINTER.
        DATA DIVISION.
        WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
        01 restart-value pic s9(10) usage binary value 0.
        PROCEDURE DIVISION.
        ST.
             call ΓÇÖUCOB_RESTARTCHECKΓÇÖ using restart-value.
             if restart-value is equal to 0
                display ΓÇÖThis execution was loaded by a normal program loadΓÇÖ upon printer.
             if restart-value is equal to 1
                display ΓÇÖThis execution is a TIP RESTARTΓÇÖ upon printer.
             if restart-value is equal to 2



11ΓÇô6                                                                               7831 0455ΓÇô022
                                                           Transaction Processing in UCS




                   display ΓÇÖThis execution is an HVTIP RESTARTΓÇÖ upon printer.
                if restart-value is equal to 3
                   display ΓÇÖThis execution was loaded by a TIP BT-Load ΓÇÖ
                 upon printer.
             EXIT PROGRAM.


11.5. Considerations
         You must observe the following restrictions in your UCS COBOL source program to
         execute it successfully in a transaction processing environment:

         ∩é╖   The local variables of a program that is loaded by either a TIP BT-Load or a TIP
             RESTART will have the values left by the previous execution. Therefore, they may
             not have the initial values from any VALUE clauses. However, if you use the
             INITIAL clause on the PROGRAM-ID statement, then the local variables are put in
             their initial state each time the program is called. Use of the INITIAL clause is
             recommended if your transaction is loaded by TIP BT-Load or TIP RESTART.
         ∩é╖   The CANCEL verb should not be used in the TIP environment, but it is supported in
             the HVTIP environment.
         ∩é╖   Report writer modules are not allowed in a TIP environment.
         ∩é╖   See the UCS Application Development Programming Guide, for details on the
             COBOL CALL identifier statement in the TIP/HVTIP environment.

Section 12
Contingency Handling

         Contingency handling is a service that notifies you when abnormal, illegal, or
         unexpected conditions occur. Contingency handlers must be registered with the Exec.
         For UCS COBOL, the interfaces to contingency registration routines and handlers are
         written as UCS COBOL-callable language program constructs. This section describes
         these interfaces.

         The URTS-supplied user contingency handling interfaces and PADS are not compatible.
         Do not link PADS into programs that have user contingency handling interfaces.
         However, if you have your own contingency handler, you still can use PADS to
         perform postmortem debugging by using the diagnostic file, DIAG$, created by the
         Exec. For example, after executing your program and capturing the storage limits
         error, you can issue a @PMD command and the Exec will call PADS and invoke a
         canned PADS dump procedure. This dump will include a register dump, walkback, and
         bank dump for the last contingency. If you want to use PADS for further debugging,
         reexecute the program followed by an @PADS DIAG command. This allows you to
         enter PADS commands. For example, to dump the jump stack, enter INQUIRE JUMPS.

         To use the UCS COBOL interfaces to contingency handling, you must be familiar with

         ∩é╖   Extended mode contingency handling
         ∩é╖   Extended mode gate and bank management
         ∩é╖   Extended mode operating environment, including the concepts of rings and
             domains

         See the System Services Programming Reference Manual for more information.

         Note that the UCS Runtime System does not verify either the contingency handling
         input parameters of the interface routines or the contents of the
         contingency registration packet.

         Status return variables from the contingency interfaces are either 2-word or 3-word
         integer values as follows:

         ∩é╖   2-word values (including the last 2 words of the 3-word value) are the return
             status information from an extended mode Exec call, except where noted. See the
             System Services Programming Reference Manual for specific Exec interface
             returns in registers A0 and A1.
         ∩é╖   3-word values are for contingency registration. The first word is a prefix that
             describes the format of the remaining 2-word value.



7831 0455ΓÇô022                                                                                  12ΓÇô1
Contingency Handling




        Two versions for registering contingencies are available as follows:
        1.    If you are using any type of registration, you can use the REG4CGY-COB2,
              CREG4CGY-COB2, or PREG4CGY-COB2 interfaces. Unisys recommends using
              these interfaces.
        2.    If you are using the version zero or version 2 registration types without using
              additional registration attributes you can use REG4CGY-COB, CREG4CGY-COB, or
              PREG4CGY-COB interfaces.

12.1. User Contingency Handler Registration
        The user contingency handler registration interfaces register the calling subsystem for
        contingency handling. You can call these interfaces from the home subsystem or from
        a shared subsystem. See the Linking System Subsystems Programming Guide for
        information on subsystem types and attributes.
        The extended mode Exec interface used is REG4CGY$.

12.1.1. Contingency Registration Packet Interface
        Interface Names
             REG4CGY-COB2 (for home subsystems)
             PREG4CGY-COB2 (for protected subsystems)
             CREG4CGY-COB2 (for chameleon subsystems)

        The parameters in the following call setup example are the same for each interface
        name.

        Call Setup
        Note: A common parameter list is used by all interfaces.

       :
       COPY CGY-REG.
       :
       01   name      PIC X(n).
       01   namelen   PIC S9(10) USAGE BINARY VALUE n.
       01   locality PIC S9(10) USAGE BINARY.
       01   priv      PIC S9(10) USAGE BINARY.
       01   ring      PIC S9(10) USAGE BINARY.
       01   status01.
            02 stat   PIC S9(10) USAGE BINARY OCCURS 3 TIMES.
       :
            CALL "REG4CGY-COB2" USING name, namelen, cgy-reg-pkt, cgy-pkt-size, locality,
                                     priv, ring, status01.

        where:

        name

              The name of the user contingency handling routine. It is processed as a character
              string by the registration interface routine. (n is the length in characters of the
              contingency handling routine name.)



12ΓÇô2                                                                               7831 0455ΓÇô022
                                                                         Contingency Handling




         namelen

             The length in bytes of the user contingency handling routineΓÇÖs name. It is
             processed as an integer value by the registration interface routine.

         cgy-reg-pkt

             The address of the contingency registration packet. See the Exec Systems
             Services PRM under contingency registration REG4CGY$ for details.

         cgy-pkt-size

             The size in words of the contingency registration packet.

         locality

             The address tree level of the gate created for the contingency handler. Allowable
             values are

                0 CallerΓÇÖs level (default)
                1 Application level
                2 Program level
                3 Activity level
                5 CallerΓÇÖs level
         priv

             The processor privilege at which the contingency handler executes. Allowable
             values are

                0 Ordinary user (default)
                2 Proprietary user
                3 Ordinary user
         ring

             The ring level of the gate created for the contingency handler. Allowable values
             are

                0 Ring 3 (default)
                2 Ring 2
                3 Ring 3




7831 0455ΓÇô022                                                                               12ΓÇô3
Contingency Handling




        status

           A 3-word integer value containing the registration status that is returned. If the
           first word returned is zero, registration was successful. If the first word is not
           zero, registration failed, and the first word describes the format for the last 2-word
           value as shown in the table that follows.


                  First Word                                Description

                      0        Registration completed normally.
                      1        The contingency gate could not be created.
                               The 2-word value is the status returned from the Exec CREATE$GATE
                               interface.
                      2        The contingency registration with the Exec failed. The 2-word value is
                               the status returned from the Exec REG4CGY$ interface.
                      3        User contingency handling entry point address is invalid. The 2-word
                               value is invalid.


        Contingency Registration Packet
        The following contingency registration packet definitions are found in the Unisys
        system PROC file (SYS$LIB$*PROC$). The PROC name is CGY-PKTS. See the System
        Services Programming Reference Manual for a complete description of field
        definitions and meanings.

        CGY-REG PROC
               01 CGY-REG-PKT.
                   05 cgy-version                       PIC S9(5) USAGE BINARY VALUE 2.
                   05 cgy-function                      PIC S9(5) USAGE BINARY VALUE 30.
                   05 cgy-penetrate                     PIC 1(36) USAGE BINARY-1 VALUE 0.
                   05 cgy-reserved                      PIC 1(30) USAGE BINARY-1 VALUE 0.
                   05 cgy-boundary                      PIC 1(6) USAGE BINARY-1 VALUE 0.
               01 CGY-PKT-SIZE                          PIC S9(10) USAGE BINARY VALUE 3.
         END

12.1.2. Contingency Registration Version or Function Interface
        Interface Names
          REG4CGY-COB (for home subsystems)
          PREG4CGY-COB (for protected subsystems)
          CREG4CGY-COB (for chameleon subsystems)

        The parameters in the following call setup example are the same for each interface
        name.

         Call Setup
         Note: A common parameter list is used by all interfaces.

          :
          01      name      PIC X(n).
          01      namelen   PIC S9(10) USAGE BINARY VALUE n.
          01      func.
                  05 version        PIC 9(5) USAGE BINARY
                  05 function-code PIC 9(5) USAGE BINARY
          01      locality PIC S9(10) USAGE BINARY.
          01      priv      PIC S9(10) USAGE BINARY.
          01      ring      PIC S9(10) USAGE BINARY.
          01      status01.
                  02 stat   PIC S9(10) USAGE BINARY OCCURS 3 TIMES.
          :
                  CALL "REG4CGY-COB" USING name, namelen, func, locality,
                                           priv, ring, status01.

         where:

         name

               The name of the user contingency handling routine. It is processed as a character
               string by the registration interface routine. (n is the length in characters of the
               contingency handling routine name.)

         namelen

               The length in bytes of the user contingency handling routineΓÇÖs name. It is
               processed as an integer value by the registration interface routine.

         func

               The type of contingency registration. The only allowable values are


                       Value                               Description

                         10       Extended mode contingency registration.
                         30       Extended mode contingency registration with additional coverage
                                  for unregistered subsystems and AFCBs that are called from the
                                  subsystem in which this registration is being done.

               This field contains two half-word binary fields (9(5) BINARY). The first PIC 9(5)
               BINARY field is the version. Version 0 supports word 0 of the contingency packet
               only. Version 1 supports words 0 to 2 with words 1 and 2 being set to zero.
               Passing registration attributes are not allowed. Version 2 indicates that the
               registering subsystem is prepared to handle the additional contingency
               information that can be passed to an extended mode contingency routine in
               CGY_PKT1 and CGY_PKT2. See the Systems Services Programming Reference
               Manual under contingency registration REG4CGY$ for details.

12.1.3. Contingency Packet Processing
         When a contingency occurs the Exec passes the registered contingency handler
         parameters that describe the execution environment at the time of the contingency.

         The following contingency packet definitions are found in the Unisys system PROC file
         (SYS$LIB$*PROC$). The PROC name is CGY-PKTS. See the System Services
         Programming Reference Manual for a complete description of field definitions and
         meanings.

12.2. User Contingency Handler Deregistration
         The user contingency handler deregistration interface deregisters a contingency
         handler.

         The extended mode Exec interface used is REG4CGY$ with function code 20.

         Interface Name
           DREG4CGY-COB

         Call Setup
             :
             01   status01.
                  02 stat      PIC S9(10) USAGE BINARY OCCURS 2 TIMES VALUE 0.
             :
                  CALL "DREG4CGY-COB" USING status01.

         where status is a 2-word integer value that contains the deregistration status that is
         returned. If the first word is zero, deregistration is successful. If the first word is not
         zero, deregistration failed. See the System Services Programming Reference Manual
         for specific REG4CGY$ status codes and definitions.


12.3. User Termination Handler Registration
         The user termination handler registration interface registers a handler for program and
         activity termination. This interface can be called from the home subsystem or from a
         shared subsystem. The termination handler registration is performed on a per activity
         basis.

         The extended mode Exec interface used is REG4TERM$.

         Interface Name
           REG4TERM-COB

         Call Setup
           :
           01     name            PIC X(n).
           01     namelen         PIC S9(10) USAGE BINARY VALUE n.
           01     termid          PIC S9(10) USAGE BINARY.
           01     termdata        PIC S9(10) USAGE BINARY.
           01     termbuff.
                  02   buff       PIC S9(10) USAGE BINARY OCCURS 11 TIMES VALUE 0.
           01     termstat.
                  02   stat       PIC S9(10) USAGE BINARY OCCURS 2 TIMES VALUE 0.
           :
                  CALL "REG4TERM-COB" USING name, namelen, termid, termdata,
                                            termbuff, termstat.




7831 0455ΓÇô022                                                                                  12ΓÇô11
Contingency Handling




        where:

        name

           The name of the termination handling routine. It is processed as a character string
           by the termination interface routine. (n is the length in characters of the
           termination handling routine name.)

        namelen

           The length in bytes of the termination handling routine. It is processed as an
           integer value by the termination interface routine.

        termid

           A 1-word integer value that contains the termination registration identification. This
           parameter identifies the termination handler for this subsystem to the Exec. This
           value is passed to the user termination handling routine.

        termdata

           A 1-word binary value that is passed to the user termination handling routine.

        termbuff

           An 11-word contiguous data area used by the UCS Runtime System to construct
           the packet needed to invoke the user termination handling routine with the proper
           parameters and UCS execution environment. This is the buffer that must be
           passed to the termination registration interface routine as an input parameter. The
           UCS Runtime System constructs the contents of this buffer. Only the space (11
           contiguous words) needs to be provided. The buffer should not be modified
           between registration and invocation of the termination routine.

        termstat

           A 2-word integer value that contains the termination registration status that is
           returned. If the first word returned is zero, termination registration was
           successful. If the first word is not zero, registration failed and the first word of the
           status field contains the following information:

           H1 nonzero
                 Status value is from REG4TERM$ call. See the System Services Programming
                 Reference Manual for REG4TERM$ status codes and definitions.
                 Status value is from REG4TERM$ call.

           H1 zero
                 H2 contains the status from the Linking System interface LS$RES_NAME (see
                 the Linking System Programming Reference Manual).

12.4. User Termination Handler Deregistration
        The user termination handler deregistration interface deregisters a termination
        handler.

        The extended mode Exec interface used is REG4TERM$.

        Interface Name
            DREG4TERM-COB

        Interface Setup
            :
            01      termid PIC S9(10) USAGE BINARY.
            01      termstat.
                    02   stat PIC S9(10) USAGE BINARY OCCURS 2 TIMES.
            :
                    CALL "DREG4TERM-COB" USING termid, termstat.

        where:

        termid

                The termination handler that is to be deregistered. It must be the same value
                passed to the termination registration interface registration routine.

        termstat

                A 2-word integer value that contains the termination deregistration status that is
                returned. If the first word is zero, the termination deregistration was successful. If
                the first word is not zero, the termination deregistration failed. See the System
                Services Programming Reference Manual for REG4TERM$ status codes and
                definitions.


12.5. UCS Runtime System Contingency Handling
        UCS Runtime System contingency handling is described in the following subsections:

        ∩é╖       Home Subsystem Operation
        ∩é╖       Shared Subsystem Restrictions




12ΓÇô14                                                                                  7831 0455ΓÇô022
                                                                       Contingency Handling




12.5.1. Home Subsystem Operation
         UCS COBOL has processing or language features that depend on the contingency
         handling provided by the UCS Runtime System in the home subsystem. If you register
         for and handle home subsystem contingencies, it can have an effect on the operation
         of the program. In addition to the special contingency processing in the following list,
         the UCS Runtime System displays a contingency message for all other contingencies
         that occur and then performs standard action (program execution is not resumed).

         The following list shows the areas of processing that are dependent on special URTS
         contingency handling, which includes processing a contingency interrupt and then
         resuming program execution:

         ∩é╖   Arithmetic faults with ON SIZE ERROR clause. The UCS Runtime System sets flag
             indicating arithmetic fault occurrence and resumes program execution.
         ∩é╖   CALL IDENTIFIER with ON OVERFLOW clause (non-ZOOM case). The UCS Runtime
             System sets flag for generated code in the NOFIND case and resumes program
             execution.

12.5.2. Shared Subsystem Restrictions
         The areas of processing and language features listed as being dependent upon the
         UCS Runtime System contingency processing in the home subsystem will not function
         similarly in a shared subsystem environment. The UCS Runtime System must capture
         contingencies in order to process them. This is not possible since the UCS Runtime
         System is registered for the home subsystem and the actual contingency occurs in
         the shared subsystem.

Contingency Handling

Section 13
Processing Tapes for Exchanging
Information

         The UCS COBOL Information Interchange Tape Processing module aids the porting of
         files to or from a system manufactured by another company. This module processes
         tapes that adhere to the X3.27-1969 Magnetic Tape Labels for Information Interchange.
         This standard is the preferred format for exchanging data between the systems of
         different computer manufacturers.

         This section contains the Unisys definition of rules and restrictions for the processing
         of tapes that adhere to the Magnetic Tape Labels standard. These formats are in
         addition to, and in some cases, replacements for the formats, syntax, and rules for
         sequential I-O that are described in the UCS COBOL Programming Reference Manual
         Volume 1.

         The information in this section applies to the following UCS COBOL divisions:

         ∩é╖    Environment Division
         ∩é╖    Data Division

         This section uses the same organization as the sequential I-O section to help you
         determine where the Magnetic Tape Labels standard differs from the standard for
         COBOL85.


13.1. Environment DivisionΓÇöInput-Output Section
         The Input-Output Section is part of the Environment Division of a source program. The
         Input-Output Section deals with the information the system needs to control
         transmission and handling of data between external media and the object program.
         The Input-Output Section is optional in the Environment Division of a COBOL source
         program.

13.1.1. The FILE-CONTROL Paragraph
         Function
         The FILE-CONTROL paragraph names each file and allows specification of other
         file-related information.

         General Format
             FILE-CONTROL .    { file-control-entry } . . .



7831 0455ΓÇô022                                                                                13ΓÇô1
Processing Tapes for Exchanging Information




13.1.2. The File Control Entry
        Function
        The file control entry names a file and can specify other file-related information.

        General Format




        Syntax Rules
        1.   The SELECT clause must be specified first in the file control entry. The clauses that
             follow the SELECT clause can appear in any order.
        2.   Each file name in the Data Division must be specified only once in the
             FILE-CONTROL paragraph. Each file name specified in the SELECT clause must
             have a file description entry in the Data Division of the same program.
        3.   The only allowable implementor-name-1 is INTERCHANGE.
        4. If implementor-name-2 is specified, it is a 1- to 12-character name used to link the
           COBOL file to OS 2200 Executive File Control and should appear on an @ASG or
           @USE statement in the runstream for executing the object program.
        5.   When implementor-name-2 is not specified, the first 12 characters of file-name-1
             are used to link the COBOL file to the OS 2200 Executive File Control.
        6. All recursions of implementor-name-2 are for documentation only.
        7.   If the ACCESS MODE clause is not specified, sequential access is assumed.
        8. Data-name-1 must be defined in the Data Division as a 2-character data item of the
           category alphanumeric and must not be defined in the File Section, the Report
           Section, or the Communication Section. Data-name-1 must be defined as USAGE
           DISPLAY.
        9. Data-name-1 can be qualified.
        10. When the ORGANIZATION IS SEQUENTIAL clause is not specified, sequential
            organization is implied.
        11. The OPTIONAL phrase applies only to files opened in the input mode. Its
            specification is required for input files that are not necessarily present each time
            the object program is executed.


13ΓÇô2                                                                               7831 0455ΓÇô022
                                              Processing Tapes for Exchanging Information




         General Rules
         1.   The ASSIGN clause specifies the association of the file referred to by file-name-1
              with a storage medium.
         2.   If the RESERVE clause is specified, it is for documentation only. Two input-output
              areas are always allocated.
         3.   The ORGANIZATION clause specifies sequential organization as the logical
              structure of a file. The file organization is established at the time a file is created
              and cannot subsequently be changed.
         4. Records in the file are accessed in the sequence dictated by the file organization.
            This sequence is specified by predecessor-successor record relationship
            established by the execution of WRITE statements when the file is created or
            extended.
         5.   If the FILE STATUS clause is specified, the data item referred to by data-name-1 is
              always updated to contain the value of the I-O status following an I-O operation.


13.2. Data DivisionΓÇöFile Section
         In a COBOL program the File Description (FD) entry represents the highest level of
         organization in the File Section. The File Section header is followed by a file description
         entry consisting of a level indicator (FD), a file name, and a series of independent
         clauses. The FD clauses specify the size of the logical and physical records, the
         presence or absence of label records, the value of label items defined by Unisys, and
         the names of the data records that comprise the file. The entry itself is terminated by
         a period.

13.2.1. The RECORDING MODE Clause
         Function
         The RECORDING MODE clause is used to specify a tape format specified in X3.27-1978
         Magnetic Tape Labels and File Structures for Information Interchange.

         General Format




         RECORDING ßê╛ MODE IS ßê┐ α╡₧ α╡ó
                                D
                                F
                                S
                                U

         General Rules
         The structure of the physical data blocks can be defined by one of the following:

         1.   The D phrase specifies variable-length blocked records.
         2.   The F phrase specifies fixed blocked records.
         3.   The S phrase specifies spanned blocked records.
         4. The U phrase specifies variable-length unblocked records.

13.2.2. Record Description Restrictions
        Data items in a record description for an INTERCHANGE file abide by the following
        restrictions:

        ∩é╖   The usage for each data item must be DISPLAY.
        ∩é╖   The description of each signed numeric data item must include the SIGN IS
            LEADING SEPARATE CHARACTER clause.

Section 14
Processing IBM Tapes

         Unisys tape formats differ from those used by IBM. Thus, if you use IBM tapes to
         input or output data, you need to attain compatibility between the two formats by
         adapting your program to use the IBM Tape Processing Module as described in this
         section.

         This section contains the rules and restrictions for processing IBM tapes. These
         formats are in addition to, and in some cases, replacements for the formats, syntax,
         and rules for sequential I-O that are described in the UCS COBOL Programming
         Reference Manual Volume 1. The information applies to the following UCS COBOL
         divisions:

         ∩é╖   Environment Division
         ∩é╖   Data Division
         ∩é╖   Procedure Division

         This section uses the same organization as the sequential I-O section in the UCS
         COBOL Programming Reference Manual Volume 1 to help you determine the special
         requirements for processing IBM tapes.


14.1. Function
         The IBM Tape Processing module can access records of an IBM-formatted tape file in
         an established sequence. The sequence is established as a result of writing the
         records to the file. It also provides for the specification of rerun points and the sharing
         of storage areas among files.


14.2. Language Concepts
         The following subsections describe the language considerations that apply to
         processing IBM tapes.

14.2.1. Organization
         Each record of a sequential file except the first has a unique predecessor record, and
         each record except the last has a unique successor record. These
         predecessor-successor relationships are established by the order of WRITE
         statements when the file is created. Once established, the predecessor-successor
         relationships do not change.




7831 0455ΓÇô022                                                                                   14ΓÇô1
Processing IBM Tapes




14.2.2. Access Mode
        In the sequential-access mode, the sequence in which records are accessed is the
        order in which the records were originally written.

14.2.3. File Position Indicator
        The file position indicator is a conceptual entity used to specify the next record to be
        accessed within a given file. The concept of the file position indicator has no meaning
        for a file opened in the output mode. The setting of the file position indicator is
        affected only by the OPEN and READ statements.

14.2.4. The At-End Condition
        The at-end condition can occur as a result of the execution of a READ statement. For
        details of the causes of the condition, see 14.5.3.

14.2.5. Allocation Listing
        The Allocation Listing gives information about variables and labels. Storage allocation
        of programs that use IBM tape processing is converted when records are read or
        written. The Allocation Listing reflects the internal allocations of the UCS COBOL
        compiler, not the IBM record allocation.


14.3. Environment DivisionΓÇöInput-Output Section
        The Input-Output Section is part of the Environment Division of a source program.
        The Input-Output Section deals with the information the system needs to control
        transmission and handling of data between external media and the object program.
        The Input-Output Section is optional in the Environment Division of a COBOL source
        program.

14.3.1. The FILE-CONTROL Paragraph
        Function
        The FILE-CONTROL paragraph names each file and allows specification of other
        file-related information.

        General Format
          FILE-CONTROL .      { file-control-entry } ...

         SELECT  OPTIONAL   ΓêÆ  

         Syntax Rules
         1.     The SELECT clause must be specified first in the file control entry. The clauses
                following the SELECT clause can appear in any order.
         2.     Each file described in the Data Division must be named only once as file-name in
                the FILE-CONTROL paragraph. Each file specified in the file control entry must
                have a file description entry in the Data Division.
         3.     The implementor-name-1 is TAPE.
         4. If the implementor-name-2 is specified, it is a 1- to 12-character name used to link
            the COBOL file to OS 2200 system Exec file control and should appear on an
            @ASG or @USE statement in the runstream for executing the object program.
         5.     If the implementor-name-2 is specified, it is a 1- to 12-character name used to link
                the COBOL file to system Exec file control and should appear on an @ASG or
                @USE statement in the runstream for executing the object program.
         6. When implementor-name-2 is not specified, the first 12 characters of the file
            name are used to link the COBOL file to system Exec file control.
         7.     All recursions of implementor-name-1 and implementor-name-2 are for
                documentation only.
         8. If the ACCESS MODE clause is not specified, the ACCESS MODE IS SEQUENTIAL
            clause is implied.
         9. When the ORGANIZATION IS SEQUENTIAL clause is not specified, the
            ORGANIZATION IS SEQUENTIAL clause is implied.

             required for input files that are not necessarily present each time the object
             program is executed.
