          *
              OPEN-OUTPUT-FILE.
                  MOVE 0 TO CIFS-MODE.
                  COMPUTE CIFS-MODE-IRWXU = CIFS-MODE-IREAD +
                                            CIFS-MODE-IWRITE.
                  COMPUTE CIFS-MODE-IRWXG = CIFS-MODE-IREAD;
                  COMPUTE CIFS-MODE-IRWXO = CIFS-MODE-IREAD;
                  CALL "CIFS$CREAT" USING ARGUMENT-2,
                                          CIFS-MODE,
                                          WRITE-FD,
                                          CIFS-STATUS.
                  IF WRITE-FD < 0
                      CALL "CIFS$FPRINTF" USING BYTES-WRITTEN,
                                                CIFS-STDERR-FILE,
                                                OPEN-ERROR-FORMAT,
                                                ARGUMENT-2
                      CALL "CIFS$PERROR" USING CIFS-STATUS
                      CALL "CIFS$CLOSE" USING READ-FD,
                                              CIFS-STATUS
                      GO TO COPY-DONE
                  END-IF.
          *
          *     Both input and output files are open, so start reading and writing.
          *     Display a message and punt if any errors encountered.
          *
              COPY-INPUT-TO-OUTPUT.
                  MOVE 0 TO BYTES-TOTAL.
                  PERFORM TEST AFTER UNTIL BYTES-READ = 0
                      CALL "CIFS$READ" USING READ-FD,
                                              DATA-BUFFER,
                                              131072,
                                              BYTES-READ,
                                              CIFS-STATUS
                      IF BYTES-READ < 0
                          CALL "CIFS$PERROR" USING CIFS-STATUS,
                                                    READ-ERROR-MESSAGE
                          GO TO CLOSE-FILES
                      END-IF
                      IF BYTES-READ > 0
                          CALL "CIFS$WRITE" USING WRITE-FD,
                                                   DATA-BUFFER,
                                                   BYTES-READ,
                                                   BYTES-WRITTEN,
                                                   CIFS-STATUS
                          IF BYTES-WRITTEN < 0
                               CALL "CIFS$PERROR" USING CIFS-STATUS,
                                                        WRITE-ERROR-MESSAGE
                               GO TO CLOSE-FILES
                          END-IF
                          ADD BYTES-WRITTEN TO BYTES-TOTAL
                      END-IF
                  END-PERFORM.

Section 18
XML Generator

         Generating an XML file that describes the layout of data in a COBOL 01 record can be
         used to process data when it is accessed outside of a COBOL program. For example,
         there might be a need to process record data written to an OS 2200 file on a Windows
         or Linux system. The information in the generated XML file can then be used to
         interpret the record data.


18.1. Creating an XML File
         UCS COBOL will create an XML file for a specified 01 data record with the use of the
         keyword option XML/name, where name is the name of the file that contains the
         record names for which XML files are to be produced. Optionally, this file can contain
         the CIFS path location of the XML file and an alternate name (different from the record
         name).

18.1.1. Create Record Name File
         Assume that the COBOL program, cobex, contains the following data descriptions in
         Working-Storage:

                IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
                PROGRAM-ID. cobex.
                ENVIRONMENT DIVISION.
                CONFIGURATION SECTION.
                SOURCE-COMPUTER. UNISYS-2200.
                OBJECT-COMPUTER. UNISYS-2200.
                DATA DIVISION.
                WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
                01 cobrec1.
                    02 dn1 PIC XXX.
                    02 dn2 PIC 99.
                01 cobrec2.
                    02 dn3 PIC S99v99.
                    02 dn4 PIC $$$9.9.
                01 cobrec3.
                    02 dn5 PIC 9(10) BINARY.
                    02 dn6 PIC X.
                PROCEDURE DIVISION.
                BEGIN.
                     :
                     :




7831 0455ΓÇô022                                                                               18ΓÇô1
XML Generator




       To create an XML file (it will have .xsd extension) for the three 01 data records in this
       program, a file must be created that specifies these record names. In addition, this file
       can optionally contain the CIFS location and alternate name of the resultant .xsd file.
       LetΓÇÖs create a text file called recnames and place the following information into it:

       cobrec1
       cobrec2 /os2200/bek/xmlwork/xyz
       cobrec3 abc

       In this example, .xsd files for the COBOL record names cobrec1, cobrec2 and cobrec3
       will be generated. Since no CIFS path was specified for cobrec1, by default, the file
       cobrec1.xsd will be placed into the CIFS current working directory (as setup by
       CIFSUT). The CIFS current working directory can be determined by using the pwd or
       cd command in the CIFSUT utility. The record name cobrec2 has an absolute path (path
       starts with a ΓÇÿ/ΓÇÖ) associated with it so, the file xyz.xsd will be created in the path
       /os2200/bek/xmlwork (this path must exist otherwise an error will be issued). This file
       will contain the information for the COBOL record cobrec2. The record name cobrec3
       has a relative path (path does NOT start with a ΓÇÿ/ΓÇÖ) associated with it, so the file
       abc.xsd will be created and placed into the CIFS current working directory.

       Note: If the same CIFS absolute path is specified for multiple 01 records, then only
       the last occurrence in the record names file will cause an .xsd XML file to be
       generated.

18.1.2. Pre-compilation Setup
       Before the compilation can be performed, the CIFS current working directory must be
       established and the file (created above) that contains the record names to process
       must be placed into it. To set the CIFS current working directory, do the following:

       >@cifsut
       CIFSUT 8R2Q1 (2014-Jul-29 20:27:13)    2015-Feb-03 Tue 11:41:59
       >cd /os2200/bek/xmldump
       >pwd
       /os2200/bek/xmldump
       >ls
       cobex

       The pwd command shows that the CIFS current working directory has been set to
       /os2200/bek/xmldump. In OS 2200 terminology this is the program file bek*xmldump.
       The ls command displays the contents of that directory, which is the COBOL source
       program cobex (see Section 18.1.2) that is to be compiled.

       Now the file (recnames) that contains the data records to process must be copied into
       the CIFS current working directory. There are several ways to do this (@copy,s,
       CIFSUT cp command, or copy/paste from Windows Explorer). The following illustrates
       using the CIFSUT cp command:

       >@cifsut
       >cp /os2200/q/f/recnames    /os2200/bek/xmldump/recnames




18ΓÇô2                                                                            7831 0455ΓÇô022
                                                                                   XML Generator




         >ls /os2200/bek/xmldump
         cobex    recnames

         As you can see, the directory now contains the COBOL source program (cobex) to
         compile as well as the file (recnames) that contains the record names to process.

18.1.3. Compile the COBOL Program
         The program must now be compiled in order to get XML (.xsd) files created. The file
         containing the record names to process must be specified using the XML keyword
         option. This can be done as follows:

         >@ucob bek*xmldump.cobex,om,,,xml/recnames
         UCOB- 12.81/ EM (150126) LSS- 14.136/ 2200/8030 (150115) 2015 Feb 03 1155:17
         SIZES: CODE(EM6): 72 DATA: 110END UCOB- 0 ERRORS(MAJOR) 0 ERRORS(MINOR)

         Now, use CIFSUT to look at the contents of the directories:

         >@cifsut
         CIFSUT 8R2Q1 (2014-Jul-29 20:27:13) 2015-Feb-03 Tue 11:55:40
         >ls /os2200/bek/xmldump
         abc.xsd   cobex   COBREC1.xsd     recnames
         >ls /os2200/bek/xmlwork
         xyz.xsd

         Upon completion of the compilation, three .xsd files were created as requested by the
         recnames file. The ls command above displays the contents of these directories. The
         .xsd file for the data record cobrec1 (COBREC1.xsd) is placed into the CIFS current
         working directory (/os2200/bek/xmldump) by default. The .xsd file for the data record
         cobrec3 (abc.xsd) is also placed into the CIFS current working directory because its
         location in the record name file was specified as a relative location within the CIFS
         current working directory. The .xsd file for the data record cobrec2 (xyz.xsd) is placed
         in directory /os2200/bek/xmlwork/xyz because the location in the record name file
         was specified as an absolute location.

         NOTE: The output object module of the compilation cannot be directed to the CIFS
         current working directory (cwd) since the compiler assigns it exclusively, making it
         unavailable to CIFS. CIFS I/O is used to read the record name text file and write the
         .xsd documents, so that no other run can have the program file, which is the CIFS
         current working directory, assigned exclusively. This includes the run doing the
         UCOB compilation.

18.3. XML File names
       CIFS is used to create XML files. The CIFS file names may be based on a record name
       or on a CIFS path specified in the XML keyword option file. The XML files are
       ultimately kept in an OS 2200 program file as symbolic elements, always having a
       version name of xsd. The element name used by CIFS may not be exactly the same
       as the name you specified, instead, it may be truncated due to length or some
       characters may be changed due to element name restrictions. For example, a data
       name that contains a dash (-) will have the dash changed to an underscore (_). In
       addition, if a data name begins with a digit, an underscore is appended to the front of
       the name. A CIFSUT ls command on the directory will show the actual name that was
       created, but a FURPUR @prt,t command may show a truncated or modified name.


18.4. Back-to-Back COBOL Programs
       If the COBOL source contains back-to-back programs (multiple compilations in a single
       source) the XML/name keyword option will be in effect for each compilation. If the
       same 01 record name exists in each compilation unit, then the PROGRAM-ID of the
       program currently being compiled will be appended to the record name. For example,
       if the record name being processed is rec1 and it exists in each compilation unit then
       two .xsd files will be generated. If the PROGRAM-ID of one compilation unit is PROG1
       then the file rec1-prog1.xsd will be created. If the PROGRAM-ID of the second
       compilation unit is PROG2, then the file rec1-prog2.xsd will be created.

       For additional information on back-to-back programs, see Section 2.4 Separate
       Compilations for a Single Source Element (Back-to-Back COBOL Programs).


18.5. Nested COBOL Programs
       A COBOL source program can contain nested programs (one compilation unit with one
       or more programs embedded within the main program). If the same 01 record name is
       used in more than one of these programs, only the first occurrence in the source will
       cause an .xsd XML file to be generated.

Appendix A
Compilation-Time Diagnostic
Messages

         This appendix describes the diagnostic messages produced by the Universal
         Compiling System (UCS) compiler during the compilation process, as follows:

         ∩é╖    UCS COBOL front-end compiler messages (see A.3)
              These messages have the prefix UCOB on listings.
         ∩é╖    UCS Language Support System (LSS) messages (see A.4)
              These messages have the prefix LSS on listings.

         This appendix also describes how to use the FIPS flagging facility to monitor how
         closely a program conforms to American National Standard COBOL (see A.2).
         Appendix B lists the diagnostic messages produced during program execution.


A.1. Diagnostic Message Types and Format
         All messages are in one of the following three classes, in decreasing order of severity:

         ∩é╖    Error
         ∩é╖    Warning
         ∩é╖    Remark

         Each message class contains one or more subclasses. Table A-1 shows the
         classification of messages in decreasing order of severity and describes the meaning
         of each subclass.

         Format
             *message-class(message-subclass) product-name-message-number: message-
             text




7831 0455ΓÇô022                                                                                AΓÇô1
Compilation-Time Diagnostic Messages




        Examples
        *ERROR(MAJOR) UCOB1200: An illegal combination of keywords has been
        encountered

        *WARNING(USAGE) UCOB1437: Numeric literal must be unsigned integer

        *ERROR(FATAL) UCOB7012: RSA fatal error following

        Note: The message numbers have the prefix UCOB to distinguish them from
        execution messages produced by components of the Language Support System
        (LSS).

        *ERROR(MINOR) UCOB422: variable-name is illegally terminated with a
        hyphen -
        it is processed with the hyphen included

        Note: Italicized words in some messages indicate variables that are replaced by
        actual names or data when printed on the listing.


                   Table AΓÇô1. Diagnostic Message Classes and Subclasses


           Class        Subclass                               Meaning

         ERROR      INTERNAL        An internal error means the compilation terminated due to
                                    internal problems such as table overflow or the inability to
                                    allocate more storage. Ask your site administrator to submit a
                                    User Communication Form (UCF).

                    FATAL           A fatal error is nonrecoverable. It is a user-caused error that
                                    means the compiler exceeded its limits, resulting in premature
                                    termination.

                    MAJOR           A major error indicates that the compiler cannot reasonably
                                    assume your intent or correct the error.

                    MINOR           A minor error indicates a usage or omission error. The
                                    compiler makes a reasonable assumption of your intent,
                                    corrects the problem, and continues compiling. However,
                                    further diagnostics can result.

         WARNING    USAGE           A usage warning indicates an instance of questionable usage
                                    that nevertheless does not violate the language specifications.


                    LEVEL-type      A level warning indicates the compiler detects a
                                    nonconforming feature. The compiler issues these messages
                                    only if you specify one of the compiler keyword options for
                                    level.

         REMARK     CLARIFICATION   A clarification remark can be either informational or used to
                                    identify an anomaly which is not necessarily an error but may
                                    need to be modified. The compiler issues these messages if
                                    you specify the compiler letter option E, L, or S or the keyword
                                    option REMARK.




AΓÇô2                                                                                7831 0455ΓÇô022
                                                     Compilation-Time Diagnostic Messages




         The compiler always issues messages of class ERROR. You cannot suppress printing
         them with a compiler keyword or letter option. The compiler uses the run-condition
         word to indicate the occurrence of major, fatal, or internal errors. See 2.5 for a
         description of the run-condition word in this context.

         The compiler always issues messages of class ERROR. You cannot suppress printing
         them with a compiler keyword or letter option.

         The compiler does not produce an object module in the following cases:

         ∩é╖     The program has any fatal or nonrecoverable internal errors.
         ∩é╖     The program has any major errors while either the ERREXIT or ERRCHECK
               compiler keyword option is in effect.

         In all listings, diagnostic messages consist of groups of the following lines:

         1.    The diagnostic message
         2.    A line containing the pointer character ΓÇ£vΓÇ¥ in the column where the error begins, if
               appropriate for the message
         3.    The source line that contains the error, if possible, including the line number
               (source lines that are too long are wrapped to subsequent lines)

         If a source line contains more than one error, the first two lines of the group are
         repeated for each error, in column number order. Then the source line ends the group.

         Note: The message group contains the source line even if you specified the
         source not to be printed.

         Example
         This example shows two errors in source statement 21.

              *ERROR(MAJOR) UCOB1771: IDENTIFIER N2 is not a legal operand when used
              in a
              relational expression - expression ignored
                            v
              *ERROR(MAJOR) UCOB1602: IDENTIFIER NAME is undefined
                                            v
              21    IF n1 = n2 THEN DISPLAY name.

         For easier reference, this appendix lists only message numbers and text. It does not
         include the class and subclass, since they appear on the listing.

A.2. COBOL FIPS Flagging
        The UCS COBOL compiler contains a flagging facility that allows you to optionally
        monitor a source program at compilation time. You can specify the monitoring for the
        following:

        ∩é╖   Any COBOL subset
        ∩é╖   Optional modules
        ∩é╖   All obsolete language elements

        The monitoring is a comparison of the syntax used in the source program against the
        syntax included in the user-selected COBOL subset. The compiler diagnoses any
        syntax in the source program that does not conform to that included in the user-
        selected COBOL subset. The compiler identifies these differences through messages
        on the source program listing. The compiler also diagnoses and identifies through a
        message on the source listing any syntax for an obsolete language element that is
        included in the processor and used in the source program.

        The organization of COBOL specifications defines 12 modules. These specifications
        require eight modules:

        ∩é╖   Nucleus
        ∩é╖   Sequential
        ∩é╖   Relative
        ∩é╖   Indexed
        ∩é╖   Interprogram Communication
        ∩é╖   Sort-Merge
        ∩é╖   Source Text Manipulation
        ∩é╖   Intrinsic Functions

        The COBOL specifications define four modules that are optional:

        ∩é╖   Report Writer
        ∩é╖   Segmentation
        ∩é╖   Debug
        ∩é╖   Communication

        UCS COBOL implements all of the required modules and two of the four optional
        modules, Report Writer and Segmentation.




AΓÇô4                                                                           7831 0455ΓÇô022
                                                       Compilation-Time Diagnostic Messages




         Most modules contain either one or two levels. All components in the UCS COBOL
         Programming Reference Manual Volume 1 that are not boxed are considered level 1
         unless stated otherwise. Volume 1 identifies level 2 components by enclosing them in
         solid boxing. UCS COBOL also monitors nonstandard extensions (as denoted in
         Volume 1 by broken-line boxes). The modules and levels are arranged to create three
         subsets and a standard level. Table A-2 summarizes the relationship of the modules,
         levels, and subsets.


                               Table AΓÇô2. Modules, Levels, and Subsets


                          Module               Level Low          Level          Level       Level
                                                              Intermediate       High      Standard

         Nucleus (NUC)                             1                1               2            2
         Sequential (SEQ)                          1                1               2            2
         Relative (REL)                            -                1               2            2
         Indexed (INX)                             -                1               2            2
         Interprogram Communication (IPC)          1                1               2            2
         Sort-Merge (SRT)                          -                1               1            1
         Source Text Manipulation (STM)            -                1               2            2
         Intrinsic Functions (ITR)                 -                1               1            1
         Report Writer (RPW)                       -                -               -            1
         Segmentation (SEG)                        -                -               -            2
         Debug (DEB)                               -                -               -            2
         Communication (COM)                       -                -               -            2


         You choose the level at which the source program is monitored by specifying one of
         the following compiler keyword options on the compiler call:


                   Option                                     Description

          LEVEL/STANDARD LEVEL       LEVEL/STANDARD and LEVEL issue warning messages for
                                     nonstandard or obsolete features used within the program.
          NO-LEVEL (default)         NO-LEVEL suppresses level checking and warning messages.
          LEVEL/LOW                  LEVEL/LOW issues warning messages for nonstandard, obsolete,
                                     intermediate, high, and standard features.
          LEVEL/INTERMEDIATE         LEVEL/INTERMEDIATE issues warning messages for nonstandard,
                                     obsolete, high, and standard features.
          LEVEL/HIGH                 LEVEL/HIGH issues warning messages for nonstandard, obsolete,
                                     and standard features.




7831 0455ΓÇô022                                                                                        AΓÇô5
Compilation-Time Diagnostic Messages




                Option                                     Description

         LEVEL/OBSOLETE          LEVEL/OBSOLETE issues warning messages for obsolete
                                 features.
                                 The option STD-ERRCHECK sets LEVEL/STANDARD. Otherwise
                                 the default is NO-LEVEL.
         LEVEL/SQL               LEVEL/SQL issues warning messages for nonstandard syntax or
                                 host-variable references within an embedded SQL command.
         LEVEL/RPW               LEVEL/RPW issues messages for syntax that belong to the
                                 optional Report Writer module.
         LEVEL/SEG               LEVEL/SEG issues messages for syntax that belong to the
                                 optional Segmentation Module.
         LEVEL/SEG2              LEVEL/SEG2 issues messages for syntax that belong to level 2 of
                                 the Segmentation module.

        *WARNING(LEVEL) UCOB1101:       (subset) level syntax is NON-CONFORMING
        STANDARD

           The syntax is nonconforming standard if the nonconforming syntax is not included
           within the user-selected COBOL subset or optional modules. SUBSET indicates the
           COBOL subset in which the current syntax is allowed.

        *WARNING(NONSTANDARD) UCOB1102:        Syntax is non-conforming non-standard -
        UCOB

           The syntax is nonconforming nonstandard if the nonconforming syntax is a
           nonstandard extension included in the processor.

        *WARNING(LEVEL) UCOB1103:       (subset) level syntax does not conform to the
        level desired

           Duplicate of UCOB1101.

        *WARNING(LEVEL) UCOB1104:       This item is in the Obsolete Language list

           The syntax is obsolete if the syntax identified is in the obsolete category within a
           COBOL subset or optional module included in the processor.

                RESERVE clause is ignored. The number of buffers used by UCS COBOL at
                run time is (4 + n + a), where n = integer specified on RESERVE clause, a =
                number of alternate keys. The maximum number of buffers that can be
                used is 63, therefore if 4 + n + a > 63 the integer specified on the RESERVE
                clause will be ignored.

                A or X and at least one B, 0 or /. The size of the edited characters is also
                restricted. The maximum replication on an editing character (B, 0, /) is 999.

                ignored

                The allowable characters in a PICTURE clause are A, B, P, S, V, X, Z, CR, DB
                and their lower case equivalents, (, ), /, 0, 1, 9, +, -, *, ,, ., $, and integers
                within parentheses.

                character, + or - cannot be preceded by a floating $; the character P can
                appear only to the left or the right as a contiguous string of P's.

   2032         Illegal GLOBAL clause - GLOBAL clause is ignored

   4102         INTRESULT specified - this operation will use ASCII COBOL
                intermediate results algorithm

                The keyword option INTRESULT has been specified and the current
                statement will use the ASCII COBOL algorithm to calculate the intermediate
                results. Operations that qualify for this algorithm are * (multiply) in a
                COMPUTE statement and a DIVIDE statement that contains multiple
                receivers that have different precisions and scales. The result of doing this
                operation will be equivalent to the result that is received in ASCII COBOL.
                This result may contain less precision than the result using the standard
                UCS COBOL intermediate results algorithm.
   4103         Operation mode is float decimal, INTRESULT ignored for entire
                statement - split up statement for INTRESULT

                The COMPUTE statement contains at least one multiply (*) operator and
                one or more of the operators +, -, or /. The additional operators have
                forced the calculation mode of this statement to float decimal. The
                keyword option INTRESULT was specified, however it will be ignored for
                this statement. In order for the INTRESULT to have an affect on the
                multiply in this COMPUTE statement, the statement must be split up into
                two or more COMPUTE statements.

                beginning delimiters EXEC and SQL must be completely specified on one
                source input line.

                statement, so the statement has no effect.
  7021          BEGIN DECLARE SECTION follows another BEGIN DECLARE SECTION;
                statement is ignored

                specified range of allowable host-variables for PROCEDURE DIVISION
                embedded SQL statements follows another BEGIN DECLARE SECTION
                statement, with no intervening END DECLARE SECTION statement, so the
                statement has no effect.
  7022          Indicator variable not signed fixed integer; indicator is
                ignored

                statement must be a signed numeric item with no scale and USAGE of
                COMP, DISP or PACKED-DECIMAL. The indicator specification is ignored.
  7023          One or more COBOL host variables or indicator variables within
                an embedded SQL multi-record statement not declared properly OR
                an unsubscripted array reference used in another embedded SQL
                statement; statement is ignored

                A user array specified as a host variable or indicator variable in a multi-
                record SQL statement, such as FETCH NEXT N, must be a one-dimensional
                array with no subscripts attached, the maximum occurrence value of the
                array must be greater than or equal the value of N, and the resultant
                operand must not be edited. Conversely, an array reference without a
                subscript is not allowed as a host variable or indicator variable in other
                embedded SQL statements. In either case, the statement is ignored.

Appendix B
Execution Time Diagnostic Messages

         This appendix describes the diagnostic messages produced by a Universal Compiling
         System (UCS) COBOL program or the UCS Runtime System during the execution
         process, as follows:

         ∩é╖    UCS Runtime System messages (see B.1)
              These messages have either of the identifiers URTS or CONTINGENCY on listings.
         ∩é╖    UCS Runtime System messages for 19002 and 35001 (see B.2)
              This subsection contains special messages that can be inserted into the text for
              URTS messages 19002 and 35001, depending on the file-related error detected.
         ∩é╖    Sort/Merge messages (see B.6)
              These messages occur when the sort or merge features available to UCS COBOL
              are used.

         Format

             *message-class(message-source) message-number: message-text

         where message-source is one of the following:

         ∩é╖    UCOB
         ∩é╖    URTS
         ∩é╖    CONTINGENCY

              For this value, the following phrase may be appended to the message text:

             - in another subsystem

              This phrase indicates that the contingency actually occurred in an executing
              subsystem different from the user program or the URTS subsystem. Typically, this
              happens for one of the following reasons:

              ∩Ç¡   The contingency occurred in a basic mode alternate file common bank (AFCB),
                  since the operating system treats basic mode AFCBs as a different subsystem
                  from extended mode.
              ∩Ç¡   The contingency occurred in an extended mode subsystem different from the
                  subsystem of the user program.

           classification, format, and implementation.


B.1. UCS Runtime System Messages (URTS)
01000       Wrong index value between MERGE and RETURN statement
            The RETURN statementΓÇÖs index to the MERGE statement is greater than number
            of MERGE statements in the program.
01001       File(s) associated with report not open

            The flow of the program has reached a report writer verb before the file is
            opened.
01002       Report not INITIATED or GENERATED before TERMINATE

            The program flow has reach a TERMINATE before an INITIATE or a GENERATE of
            this report has been executed.
01003       Report not TERMINATED before INITIATE

            The program flow has reached a second INITIATE of this report before a
            TERMINATE has been executed.
01004       Report must get INITIATED before GENERATE

            The program flow has reached a GENERATE of this report before an INITIATE of
            this report has been executed.
01005       Subprogram being canceled is active - cancel not done

            The program to be canceled is still active. No CANCEL is done.
01006       Subprogram being called is active - call not completed

            The program being called is still active. No CALL is done.
01007       Number of parameters of called and callee must equal

            The number of parameters passed to the called program must not exceed the
            number of parameters it has requested.
01008       Subscript value negative or greater than OCCURS

            The value of the subscript is not within the range of the number of occurrences
            of the given identifier. This diagnostic occurs when the keyword option
            RUNCHECK is used.
01009       Reference modification starting to large or negative

            The starting point for the reference modification must be within the size of the
            identifier. This diagnostic occurs only when the keyword option RUNCHECK is
            used.
01010       Reference modification size to large or negative

            The requested size of the reference modification is larger than the remaining
            size of the identifier, or is less than one. This diagnostic occurs only when the
            keyword option RUNCHECK is used.

 07752          Array already allocated

                An attempt was made to allocate storage for an allocatable array whose storage
                had already been allocated.
                An ALLOCATE statement can be executed only for allocatable arrays whose
                storage is not currently allocated. The ALLOCATE statement cannot be used
                with:
                ∩é╖   Arrays that have never been allocated
                ∩é╖   Arrays specified in a DEALLOCATE statement that was executed prior to the
                    ALLOCATE statement
                ∩é╖   Arrays that were allocated in a subprogram but whose names did not
                    appear in a SAVE statement before execution of a RETURN or END
                    statement

 07753          Start position argument is out of range

                An attempt was made to reference a character or bit position not contained in
                the scalar variable, array element, or expression. The starting position must
                satisfy the relational expression:
                1 LE starting-pos LE item-length

                where item-length is the length of the scalar variable, array element, or
                expression.
                Refer to the FORTRAN Compiler Programming Reference Manual Volume 1 for
                a description of character substrings, the BITS, SBITS, SUBSTR, or IBITS intrinsic
                functions, or the MVBITS intrinsic subroutine.
 07755          Arrays are not conformable (extents are unequal)

                Conformable arrays were expected, but were not found when executing one of
                the following:
                ∩é╖   An array expression
                ∩é╖   An array assignment statement
                ∩é╖   A WHERE statement sequence

                 Refer to the FORTRAN Compiler Programming Reference Manual Volume 1
                for a description of conformability in array expressions, in array assignment
                statements, and in a WHERE statement sequence.
 07756          Indexed section selector subscript is out of range

                Either the first or last subscript in an indexed section selector is not in the
                allowable range for the array being referenced.
                Refer to the FORTRAN Compiler Programming Reference Manual Volume 1 for
                a description of indexed section selectors.

07757       Illegal argument passed to assumed-shape array

            An error was detected when checking for the allowable associations between
            the actual and dummy arguments. One of the following conditions occurred:
            ∩é╖   A constant or adjustable dimensioned array was passed to an assumed-
                shape array and the calling routine was not compiled with the ASHAPE
                compiler keyword option. Recompile the calling routine with the ASHAPE
                option.
            ∩é╖   An assumed-size array or a scalar value was passed to an assumed-shape
                array.

            Refer to the FORTRAN Compiler Programming Reference Manual Volume 1 for
            a description of assumed-noncontiguous arrays, assumed-size arrays, and the
            allowable associations between actual and dummy argument arrays.
07758       Bit position argument is out of range

            An attempt was made to reference a bit position not contained in a numeric
            storage unit. The following relationship must be satisfied:
            0 LE bit-position LE 35

            This error message is produced as a result of incorrectly using a BTEST, an
            IBSET, or an IBCLR intrinsic function.
            Refer to the FORTRAN Compiler Programming Reference Manual Volume 1 for
            descriptions of the BTEST, IBSET, and IBCLR intrinsic functions.
07759       Parameters are not conformable (extents are unequal)

            Conformable arrays were expected but were not found when passing
            parameters to a nonelemental intrinsic function.
            Refer to the FORTRAN Compiler Programming Reference Manual Volume 1 for
            a definition of conformability and a description of which parameters passed to a
            nonelemental intrinsic function must be conformable.
07760       An assumed-noncontiguous array can be passed only to an assumed-
            shape array

            An error was detected when checking for the allowable associations between
            the actual and dummy argument arrays. An assumed-noncontiguous array is
            illegally passed as an actual argument to a dummy argument that is not an
            assumed-shape array.
            Refer to the FORTRAN Compiler Programming Reference Manual Volume 1 for
            a description of assumed-noncontiguous arrays, assumed-size arrays, and the
            allowable associations between actual and dummy argument arrays.
07761       Intrinsic function dimension argument is out of range

            The dimension argument for an array query, array reduction, or array index
            reduction function is out of range. The following relationship must be satisfied:
                1 <= value of dimension argument <= rank of the array
            This error can also result when the dimension argument specifies the last
            dimension of an assumed-size array because the extent of the last dimension of
            an assumed-size array is undefined.

 07762          Return code from DMS 1100 is out of range

                When a call is made to DMS to execute an FDML statement, DMS returns a
                code indicating the action the program is to take after execution of the FDML
                statement. The possible actions are normal return (continue normal execution
                with the next statement), error return, at-end return, or rollback return.
 07763          RETURN from a ROLLBACK subroutine

                If an IMPART statement of the form IMPART(ROLLBACK=subr) is used and
                subroutine SUBR executes a RETURN statement, the program is terminated in
                error.
 07764          Log message length exceeds maximum of 250 words

                In the FDML LOG statement
                    LOG (length) log-area-var

                the length of the message, length, exceeds the limit of 250 words.
 07765          Character expression exceeds maximum length

                This message is issued for either of the following reasons:
                ∩é╖   A character expression that involves either of the following operands in a
                    catenation operation is restricted to 4096 characters unless the expression
                    is the source expression of an assignment statement:
                ∩é╖   An operand whose length specification is an asterisk in parentheses
                    (excluding a symbolic name of a constant)
                ∩é╖   An operand that is a substring reference, where the substring length is not
                    constant. This applies when the item meets the description in the preceding
                    bullet.
                ∩é╖   A character assignment statement of the form A = E is used where E has
                    the potential for defining character positions in A that are referenced in E,
                    and either the COMPILER statement option
                    NONSTD_CHAR_ASSIGNMENT=ON is specified or the COMPAT compiler
                    keyword option is specified. In addition, when one of the following
                    conditions exists, the compiler moves E to a temporary location before the
                    assignment to A (in which case, the expression E is restricted to 4096
                    characters in length):
                ∩é╖   E represents a concatenation operation as described in the first bullet above
                ∩é╖   E represents a substring reference as described in the second condition of
                    the first bullet above

 07766          Allocatable character array exceeds the segmented size limit

                This message is issued for the following reasons:
                ∩é╖   An ALLOCATE statement is allocating a segmented character array that
                    exceeds the 16 megaword (2**24 = 16,777,216) limit
                ∩é╖   A character array expression causes the compiler to allocate a segmented
                    character array that exceeds the 16 megaword (2**24 = 16,777,216) limit

            ∩é╖   ISHFTC: ABS(shift-count) LE field-size

                1 LE field-size LE 36

            Refer to the FORTRAN Compiler Programming Reference Manual Volume 1 for
            descriptions of the ISHFT and ISHFTC intrinsic functions.

            following relationship must be satisfied:
                1 LE field-size LE 36

            a description of the ISHFTC intrinsic function.

            greater than the length of the scalar variable, array element, or expression. The
            length must satisfy the relationship:

            where item-length is the length of the scalar variable, array element, or
            expression.
            Refer to the FORTRAN Compiler Programming Reference Manual Volume 1 for
            a description of character substrings, the BITS, SBITS, SUBSTR or IBITS intrinsic
            functions, or the MVBITS intrinsic subroutine.

            a description of character substrings, the BITS, SBITS, SUBSTR or IBITS intrinsic
            functions, or the MVBITS intrinsic subroutine.

21003       The pointer passed to the function has an offset which is invalid
            according to the function's formal parameter declaration

            UC pointers contain a word and byte offset. A pointer to char or pointer to void
            has an offset value of 0, 9, 18, or 27. A pointer to short has an offset value of 0
            or 18. A pointer to enum has an offset value of 0 or 18 if the enum is allocated
            as a short int. All other pointer types have an offset value of zero. If a pointer
            with an invalid offset is used, unexpected results can occur. When the
            RUNCHECK option is used, UC generates extra code to compare a functionΓÇÖs
            formal parameter pointer offset to the actual incoming parameterΓÇÖs pointer
            offset value. The following cases are tested:
            ∩é╖   The formal parameter is declared as pointer to short or pointer to enum
                (allocated as short int) and the byte offset of the actual parameter is not
                equal to 0 or 18.
            ∩é╖   The formal parameter is not declared as pointer to char, pointer to void,
                pointer to short, or pointer to enum (allocated as short int) and the byte
                offset of the actual parameter is not equal to 0.
21004       Pointer conversion has produced a pointer with an invalid offset

            UC pointers contain a word and byte offset. A pointer to char or pointer to void
            has an offset value of 0, 9, 18, or 27. A pointer to short has an offset value of 0
            or 18. A pointer to enum has an offset value of 0 or 18 if the enum is allocated
            as a short int. All other pointer types have an offset value of zero. If a pointer
            with an invalid offset is used, unexpected results can occur. When the

B.2. UCS Runtime System Messages for 19002 and
     35001
        The following error message text is inserted into UCS Runtime System errors 19002
        and 35001, depending on the file-related error detected. The first 3 digits are an
        internal message code used by the UCS Runtime System and are displayed as an
        index into the text below. The text for most of these errors corresponds to the PCIOS
        C2ERR or the PCIOS MSAM errors that are noted. SFS errors are displayed by the
        individual UDS error codes returned or as selected messages from the text listed here
        if they correspond to PCIOS SDF Direct or PCIOS MSAM errors.

        See the PCIOS Programming Reference Manual or the SFS Programming Reference
        Manual for further details about message descriptions.

        The following error message text is inserted into UCS Runtime System errors 19002
        and 35001, depending on the file-related error detected. The first 3 digits are an
        internal message code used by the UCS Runtime System and are displayed as an
        index into the text below. The text for most of these errors corresponds to the PCIOS
        C2ERR or the PCIOS MSAM errors that are noted. SFS errors are displayed by the
        individual UDS error codes returned, or as selected messages from the text listed
        here if they correspond to PCIOS SDF Direct or PCIOS MSAM errors. See the PCIOS
        Administration and Programming Reference Manual or the SFS Administration and
        Support Reference Manual for further details about message descriptions).

         0        Unexpected error returned by PCIOS/SFS

                  not recognized by UCS Runtime System. This most likely reflects an
                  internal error, please submit a UCF.

                  displayed as error-value.

B.3. HVTIP2/FLSS Error Messages
        The following error messages are emitted from the UCS Runtime System HVTIP
        heapmanager and FLSS nonshared data subsystem loader.

        *ERROR HVTIP2/FLSS 1: Heap bank not initialized or was corrupted.

           The heap control block constant was not found during a FREE operation. Detected
           by CDM$FREE under the name NOT_INIT_STAT. AUX = B10.

        *ERROR HVTIP2/FLSS 2: Unexpected error in the heap manager.

           A8 contains an unknown error status. Detected by ERRHANDLE under the name
           EH_ERRM2. AUX = B10.




BΓÇô66                                                                            7831 0455ΓÇô022
                                                  Execution Time Diagnostic Messages



         *ERROR HVTIP2/FLSS 3: Heap bank not initialized or was corrupted.

            The heap control block constant was not found during an ALLOCATE operation
            Detected by CDM$ALLOC under the (same) name NOT_INIT_STAT. AUX = B10.

         *ERROR HVTIP2/FLSS 4: Heap bank could not be expanded.

            An allocation was attempted but not enough contiguous space was available in
            the free chain of the requested heap bank. Either the user specified no expansion
            (SET EXPANSION_SIZE = 0) or the end of the heap bank was reached. Detected by
            CDM$ALLOC under the name STORAGE_STAT. AUX = B10.

         *ERROR HVTIP2/FLSS 5: Allocation request size is less than 2 words.

            An attempt to allocate less than two words was made. An allocation must request
            at least 2 words because 2 words are required to hold the information in a free
            chain block. Detected by CDM$ALLOC under the name TOO_SML_STAT. AUX =
            B10.

         *ERROR HVTIP2 6: Nested HVTIP Calls limit exceeded.          ReLINK ICP.

            The default HVTIP nested call limit of 8 has been reached. To get this message,
            the user must have already reconfigured the Exec for more than 8. To get more
            than 8 levels from the HVTIP2 heap manager, the ICP must be relinked specifying a
            larger BOOKKEEPING size. For example, SET BOOKKEEPING_SIZE = n. Detected by
            NEWHM under the name N_ERRM6. AUX = B10.

         *ERROR HVTIP2 7: An invalid HVTIP id was called.         The timestamps
         mismatch.

            An HVTIP ZOOM is being called again but the timestamp from the first call doesnΓÇÖt
            match the current timestamp. The ZOOM was probably updated (copied) while the
            transaction was in process. Detected by LOADSEGS under the name L_ERRM7.
            AUX = B10.

         *ERROR HVTIP2/FLSS 8: CREATE$BANK returned the following statuses:

            The HVTIP2 heap manager determined that the requested heap must be acquired
            by a CREATE$BANK Exec request. The primary and bank-specific statuses
            returned from the Exec request are printed in the error message. Detected by
            Exec function CREATE$BANK (which is called by ALLOCATESEG) under the heap
            manager name A_ERRM8. AUX = B10.

         *ERROR HVTIP2 9: CREATE$BANK returned the wrong LBDI:

            The LBDI returned by CREATE$BANK did not match the one requested by the
            HVTIP2 heap manager. Detected by ALLOCATESEG under the name A_ERRM9.
            AUX = B10.

           the field ACW_FORMAT in the ZOOMΓÇÖs Management Info structure has a value

           that supports HVTIP2. 2) Replace the ΓÇÖHVTIP2ΓÇÖ keyword from your LINK source
           OUTPUT statement with ΓÇÖHVTIPΓÇÖ and link again. Detected by Heap_Manager under
           the name O_ERRMB.

        *WARNING HVTIP2/FLSS 12: Program contains both NAMED and INDEXED common
        blocks.

           The HVTIP2 transaction contains both NAMED common blocks and INDEXED
           common blocks. The condition was first noted during the loading of the library
           bank number indicated. This is not an error but because this mixture was not
           allowed prior to HVTIP2, it may indicate a problem. Note, however, that a
           particular common block cannot be INDEXED in one ZOOM and not INDEXED in
           another ZOOM, but there is not enough information at static link time or at run
           time to detect this erroneous situation. To solve the problem (if one exists), either
           use the INDEXED COMMON BANKS statement in all or none of the HVTIP ZOOMs
           involved in the transaction, or turn off the printing of this warning. Detected by
           LOADSEGS under the name L_ERRMC.

        *HVTIP2/FLSS 13: CREATE$BANK was called by the heap manager.

           1) For an HVTIP2 ZOOM, the user has specified an LBDI that isnΓÇÖt included in one of
           the HVTIP2 VALTAB bank count specifications (for example, DSP). 2) For a FLSS,
           the user has not specified a usable heap bank for an FLSS primary heap. Turning
           on the FAST_LOAD_MONITOR (by a SET FAST_LOAD_MONITOR = n LINK
           command in the ICP LINK source or FLSS LINK source) caused this information to
           be printed. This is not an error. It is only provided to inform you that a
           performance improvement should be possible if, for HVTIP, the VALTAB is
           appropriately modified (for example, increasing the DSP small program-level bank
           count value to include the indicated L,BDI), or, for nonHVTIP, specify an LBDI (in
           the SSDEF source of your FLSS) which can be used by your program. Detected by
           BANKCREATE under the name BC_ERRMD.

           Version 2 is not specified in the parameter packet (X10) that the

         *HVTIP2/FLSS 15: The ADDR of an HVTIP2 segment is in a pooled bank.

            Only nonpooled banks are intended to be used by HVTIP2 segments (data segs

            the following: 1) changing your SET LOWADR command for the given segment 2)
            changing a VALTAB bank count 3) changing one of your OUTPUT HVTIP2 pooled
            bank counts Detected by NEWHM under the name N_ERRMF.

         *HVTIP2/FLSS 16: A HVTIP FLSS is only allowed in HVTIP2 environment.

            In an HVTIP transaction, calling an FLSS subsystem is only supported if the
            environment is HVTIP2, that is, the Exec passes information to the heap manager
            using the HVTIP2 format. You must use a version of the Exec that supports
            HVTIP2 in order to use the FLSS feature. Detected by RTS$SSLOAD under the
            name SL_ERRMG.

         *HVTIP2/FLSS 17: No heap bank is available for FLSS nonshared data.

            In an HVTIP2 transaction, if an FLSS is called, and there are no more pooled banks
            with the specified locality, the ICP LINK specifies that no CREATE$BANK Exec calls
            are allowed, and the FLSS SSDEF indicates that no sharing of heaps is allowed, the
            transaction is errored. You should increase the number of pooled banks of the
            specified locality (ICP LINK OUTPUT HVTIP2 statement), specify
            ALLOW_CREATE_BANK = TRUE (ICP LINK OUTPUT HVTIP2 statement) or specify
            HEAP BANKS ARE SHARED WITH OTHER SUBSYSTEMS INCLUDING HVTIP (FLSS
            SSDEF statement). Detected by RTS$SSLOAD under the name SL_ERRMH.

         *HVTIP2 18: Improper ZOOM format.       Relink ICP using latest @LINK.

            Only BDR1, BDR3, UTILITYI and UTILITYD are allowable values for this keyword
            clause. If you want to cause ACOBΓÇÖs C$DML to be initially based you should
            specify BM_INITIALBASING,UTILITYI,C$DML in your EXECUTION command.

         29: Intercept entrypoint [EP,EP,1,FEPNAME] calls itself. See TARGET_NAME.

            The specified entrypoint and its TARGET_NAME are the same. If the intercept
            routine calls itself, the probable result is an infinite loop. You should choose a
            different name for TARGET_NAME and its HVCALLS/$MNQ counterpart.

         30: SCSS calltype entrypoint <entrypoint> must use target-type
             FIXED_GATE_LBDI and a BMRB intercept.

            You chose a CALLTYPE of SCSS_DB or SCSS_NODB or FLSS_DB or FLSS_NODB.
            Either your target-type is wrong or your intercept type (or both).

            The target-type is determined by the presence of one of the following
            ENTRYPOINT clauses:

            TARGET_NAME, HVTARGET_LB, HVTARGET_NLB, TARGET_VA, FIXED_GATE_LBDI.
            You should use the FIXED_GATE_LBDI clause.

            Intercept type is determined by the INTERCEPT_ELT TRANSLATION clause. For
            example, an ACOB2UCOB translation will produce a BMRB intercept.

C.2. Additional Limits
        The following limits are not statically determinable, but depend on the program
        environment. If these limits are encountered, you may have to make changes to your
        program.

C.2.1. Size of an Array or Common Block
        The size of a single object, such as an array or common block, is limited by the
        physical memory available for the system. The maximum size of a single object is the
        total physical memory available minus the memory used by support software such as
        the operating and linking systems, as well as the application program. The size of a
        single object is limited to 16 megawords.




CΓÇô4                                                                               7831 0455ΓÇô022
                                                                             Compiler Limits




C.2.2. Program Addresses
         The amount of actual main storage can vary. However, because program storage is
         divided into parts, known as banks, you can execute programs whose storage size
         exceeds the actual memory size. This capability is known as virtual storage.

         Virtual address space on the 2200/XPA is about 69 billion words (262,144 banks
         multiplied by 262,144 words per allocated bank descriptor index (BDI), with up to 64
         BDIs per bank). These 69 billion words are partitioned into eight sharing levels. This
         allows a program to address an area many times larger than the physical main storage.

         For 2200/XPA systems, a program can execute if only a subset of the program banks
         resides in main storage at one time. Since these systems support hardware paging,
         only a small segment of each bank currently addressed during execution must fit into
         real memory.

         A data bank (D-bank) can be of varying size depending on its use. The entire bank need
         not be loaded into memory when addressed by the program. Small segments of the
         bank are loaded and unloaded as needed.

         By default, the compiler produces one I-bank for a compilation unit. The size of an I-
         bank produced from compiling one compilation unit can be up to 262,143 words. If you
         encounter this limit, split the program into smaller, separate compilation units or use
         the SEGCODE compiler keyword option. The SEGCODE option creates multiple I-banks
         with each I-bank having a limit of 262,143 words.

         When merging I-banks during the linking process, the merged I-bank can also contain
         up to 262,143 words (see the description of the SEGCODE processor option in Section
         2).

C.2.3. Expression Evaluation
         Compile time expression processing utilizes a push-down expression stack. As
         statement constructs such as identifiers, operators, and parentheses are recognized, a
         frame size is allocated on the stack. A stack frame is freed when the statement
         construct(s) can be processed by the compiler. This depends on the hierarchy of
         operators, use of parentheses, and what is currently being processed. Conditions that
         exceed the stack limit are diagnosed with a major error. The expression must be
         simplified in order for it to be compiled error free.

         Only one condition can exceed the stack size: nested parentheses. In the simplest
         form, an expression can have 50 left parentheses before any intermediate text needs
         to be generated. This number is reduced by whatever expression constructs are
         currently active on the stack. Also, the items within the nested parentheses require
         stack space.

         Because of recursive processing of expressions by the compiler, internal compiler
         stack space can run out. Thus text entries can only be nested 155 levels. Ways to
         simplify the statement include breaking the statement into two or more statements or
         inserting parentheses into the statementΓÇÖs expressions.




7831 0455ΓÇô022                                                                               CΓÇô5
Compiler Limits




C.2.4. Nested Procedure Calls
        The maximum number of nested procedure calls depends on the size of the run-time
        activity-local stack (ALS) and the stack sizes used by the nested procedures that are
        called. The default maximum size for the ALS stack is 229,376 words (0700000 octal).
        The ALS stack is a small OS 2200 Dbank and cannot exceed 0700000 words in size.

        When a procedure is entered, a frame size of 16+N words is allocated on the stack,
        where N is the amount of automatic storage required by the procedure. This includes
        all program variables and compiler-generated temporary allocations that are allocated
        automatic storage. When the procedure is exited, a frame is released. If the ALS size
        is exceeded, an error message specifying ALS stack overflow or underflow is issued.
        Handle this situation by performing the following steps:

        1.    Increase the size of the ALS stack. Normally, this is not possible, since by default
              the ALS bank has the maximum size limit.
        2.    Modify your procedures so that program variables use static storage rather than
              automatic, reduce the size of any large Working-Storage buffers, or reduce the
              number of nested calls. For more information, refer to the discussion of the
              MIN-ALS option.

        Following are the two examples, where ALS stack overflows during program
        execution.

        Example 1
        In this example the ALS stack overflow is due to the program running out of ALS
        stack.

             Example # 1, COBOL program gets an ALS overflow:

             *ERROR(CONTINGENCY) 10902: Activity-local stack overflow(AUX INFO
             000000000004)

                                      ERROR-ADR: 001006         L-BDI: 400005

             *ERROR(URTS): Runtime error termination (ER ERR$/EABT$)
              EXM   TYPE 03 CODE 02 CONT 21 REENT ADR: 001006 BDI: 000005 L,BDI:
             400005
                                     02 OCT 2008 16:27:41 CDT
              AUX INFO: 000000000004
             SYSTEM-UNIQUE ID: 040000000000000000403302




CΓÇô6                                                                                 7831 0455ΓÇô022
                                                                             Compiler Limits




         Example 2
         In this example, the Universal Data System (UDS) is called by the program and ALS
         does not have enough stack size for the UDS to function. UDS tests the amount of
         ALS stack remaining and raises an error ticket if the stack size not sufficient.

           Example #2, UDS senses insufficient ALS space remaining:

           Remaining stack space on ALS is not sufficient to complete this request
           SYSTEM=TSYS       ISPEC=HF01 STN=000000 - RDMS ERROR 8008 HAS
           OCCURRED

           RDMS AUX INFO 00000001
           PROBLEM RELATES TO THE FASTPATH COMMAND LISTED BELOW
           *ERROR 8008: Rollback code 50430 was returned from Thread
                       Control. The component was either DCS, RDM, RSM, TCS,
                       IRU, or DMR. Consult the Universal Data System (UDS)
                       Administration and Support Reference Manual
                       (7831 0737) to assist you in locating the UDS
                       Control message associated with this rollback code.

         MIN-ALS
         The program variables in the WORKING-STORAGE section are normally allocated in
         static storage in UCS COBOL. However, if the INITIAL clause is used on the
         PROGRAM-ID statement, then variables in the WORKING-STORAGE section are
         instead allocated on the Activity Local Stack (ALS). (Exception: Those 01 variables
         having the EXTERNAL clause are made into named COMMON blocks, which are
         always allocated in static storage.) The ALS stack is a small bank, with a maximum size
         of only 229,376 words (0700000 octal). If you have large buffers in the WORKING-
         STORAGE section that are causing ALS overflows (the ALS might run out of space due
         to nested calls), you can reduce the amount of ALS used in your COBOL programs by
         using the MIN-ALS keyword option on your UCOB compilations. This keyword option
         causes the compiler to allocate those local WORKING-STORAGE variables that do not
         have VALUE clauses on them in static storage instead of allocating them on the ALS. If
         the large buffers causing the overflow problem have VALUE clauses on them, remove
         the VALUE clauses and add code at the beginning of your procedures to initialize them.

         Note: The MIN-ALS keyword option has no effect on programs that do not have
         the INITIAL clause on their PROGRAM-ID statements.

C.2.5. Number of External Names in an Object Module
         The number of external references, external entry points, and common block names is
         limited by the maximum size of the object moduleΓÇÖs name table. The maximum size,
         defined by the linking system, is 262,144 words. All names associated with the object
         module are in this table. The minimum size for a name is two words, because each
         name has one word of control information and at least one word to hold the name.
         Four characters are stored per word. Thus, a 30-character name requires a nine-word
         entry-one control word and eight words for the name.

Appendix E
Label Processing

         This appendix discusses all of the file label processing that is performed on disk and
         tape files. An explanation is given of the COBOL source statements that can alter
         labeling procedures. Label formats are shown and default label values are indicated.
         The sequence of label processing events is outlined for each COBOL I-O verb
         affecting label processing.


E.1. The Label Records Clause
         When the STANDARD phrase of the LABEL RECORDS clause is specified for any file,
         explicit label information is created and maintained on the file. The COBOL user can
         control the contents or the validation of selected portions of this label information
         through the use of the VALUE OF clause.

         When the OMITTED phrase of the LABEL RECORDS clause is specified for any DISC,
         TAPE, or INTERCHANGE file, implicit label information is created and maintained on the
         file. In this case, you cannot use the VALUE OF clause to override any of the system
         default values used to create or validate this label information. However, if a TAPE or
         INTERCHANGE file is assigned with the J option, no implicit label processing occurs
         and the tape must be unlabeled.


E.2. Label Formats
         The method by which label information is recorded on a file varies with the type of file.

E.2.1. TAPE and INTERCHANGE Files
         The labels recorded on files having TAPE or INTERCHANGE as implementor-name-1 in
         the ASSIGN clause are maintained by the Tape Labeling System in the operating
         system. These labels include VOL1, HDR1, HDR2, EOF1, EOF2, EOV1, and EOV2. See the
         PCIOS Administration and Programming Reference Manual for more information.




7831 0455ΓÇô022                                                                                 EΓÇô1
Label Processing

        The VOL1 label exists as the first label block on every reel. It is maintained by the
        system Executive to verify that the proper reel has been mounted. The COBOL
        program has no access to this label.

                file name was: MYPROJECTID*CREATEDFILE, the base level inserts

                string occurs in this field for all files within a file set. In other words, all HDR1
                records for all files on a volume or multiple volumes contain the same file
                identifier in the default case. The file identifier in the default case is left-justified,
