F.4.39. I-O Statuses
       Description
       New I-O statuses have been added. The new statuses define previously undefined
       actions that could have been implemented in a variety of ways.

       Expected Impact on ASCII COBOL Programs
       Very little impact is anticipated. New statuses do not conflict with existing statuses
       but there is a possible upward compatibility problem. With the new statuses that
       have been defined, it is possible for you to detect I-O errors from the Declarative
       section of the UCS COBOL program. In UCS COBOL, when a Declarative section is
       defined, the UCS Runtime System does not issue an error message as was done in
       ASCII COBOL.


F.5. Obsolete Language Elements
       The following features are present in this level of the standard (COBOL 85), but will be
       removed from future revisions of the standard. These features are either obsolete or
       improperly specified, but it is felt their abrupt removal from the standard would be a
       disservice to COBOL users. It is strongly recommended that these features not be
       used when writing new programs.

F.5.1. Character Substitution
       Description
       Character substitution of double characters for a single UCS COBOL character has
       been placed in the obsolete category. This means that this feature will be removed
       from future revisions of the standard and should not be used when writing new
       programs.

       These specifications are a carry over from computers that could not provide the full
       UCS COBOL character set.

       Expected Impact on ASCII COBOL Programs
       No impact is anticipated. Usage is flagged at compilation time.

F.5.2. ALL Literal and Numeric or Numeric Edited Items
       Description
       The figurative constant ALL literal that is associated with a numeric or numeric edited
       item, and that has a length greater than one, has been placed in the obsolete category.
       This means that this feature will be removed from future revisions of the standard and
       should not be used when writing new programs.

       Expected Impact on ASCII COBOL Programs
       Some problems could occur.

       A diagnostic flagging this as an obsolete feature is provided.



FΓÇô34                                                                            7831 0455ΓÇô022
                                               UCS COBOL and ASCII COBOL Differences




         Changes
         Moving an ALL literal to numeric or numeric edited items when the length of the literal
         is greater than one character is allowed in UCS COBOL.

F.5.3. Identification Division Paragraphs
         Description
         The AUTHOR, INSTALLATION, DATE-WRITTEN, DATE-COMPILED, and SECURITY
         paragraphs in the Identification Division have been placed in the obsolete category.
         This means that these features will be removed from future revisions of the standard
         and should not be used when writing new programs.

         Expected Impact on ASCII COBOL Programs
         No impact is anticipated. A diagnostic flagging this as an obsolete feature is provided.

         Changes
         UCS COBOL allows these paragraphs, but ignores them. Remove or comment out
         these paragraphs.

F.5.4. MEMORY SIZE Clause
         Description
         The MEMORY SIZE clause has been placed in the obsolete category. This means it will
         be removed from future revisions of the standard and should not be used when
         writing new programs.

         This clause was totally implementor defined and there was no commonality among
         implementations which have assigned a use to the phrase. Any meaning is better left
         for the operating system to define.

         Expected Impact on ASCII COBOL Programs
         No impact is anticipated. It is not needed for programs which contain addresses over
         65,535 since all UCS COBOL code generation allows reference of data at locations
         greater than 65,535.

         A diagnostic flagging this as an obsolete feature is provided.

         Changes
         UCS COBOL allows the MEMORY-SIZE clause, but ignores it. Remove or comment out
         the MEMORY-SIZE clause.




7831 0455ΓÇô022                                                                                FΓÇô35
UCS COBOL and ASCII COBOL Differences




F.5.5. RERUN Clause
       Description
       The RERUN clause has been placed in the obsolete category. This means that this
       feature will be removed from future revisions of the standard and should not be used
       when writing new programs.

       RERUN clause implementations were not necessarily transportable. This defines an
       operating system function that should not be a part of the language definition.

       Expected Impact on ASCII COBOL Programs
       A diagnostic flagging this as an obsolete feature is provided.

       Changes
       The RERUN clause is allowed in UCS COBOL.

F.5.6. MULTIPLE FILE TAPE Clause
       Description
       The MULTIPLE FILE TAPE clause in the I-O-CONTROL paragraph of the Environment
       Division has been placed in the obsolete category. This means that this feature will be
       removed from future revisions of the standard and should not be used when writing
       new programs.

       Expected Impact on ASCII COBOL Programs
       No impact is anticipated. A diagnostic flagging this as an obsolete feature is provided.

       Changes
       The MULTIPLE FILE TAPE clause is allowed in UCS COBOL.

F.5.7. LABEL RECORDS Clause
       Description
       The LABEL RECORDS clause in the file description entry has been placed in the
       obsolete category. This means that this feature will be removed from future revisions
       of the standard and should not be used when writing new programs.

       Expected Impact on ASCII COBOL Programs
       A diagnostic flagging this as an obsolete feature is provided.

       Changes
       The LABEL RECORDS clause is allowed in UCS COBOL.

F.5.8. VALUE OF Clause
         Description
         The VALUE OF clause in the file description entry has been placed in the obsolete
         category. This means that this feature will be removed from future revisions of the
         standard and should not be used when writing new programs.

         Expected Impact on ASCII COBOL Programs
         A diagnostic flagging this as an obsolete feature is provided.

         Changes
         The VALUE OF clause is allowed in UCS COBOL.

F.5.9. DATA RECORDS Clause
         Description
         The DATA RECORDS clause in the file description entry has been placed in the
         obsolete category. This means that this feature will be removed from future revisions
         of the standard and should not be used when writing new programs.

         Expected Impact on ASCII COBOL Programs
         A diagnostic flagging this as an obsolete feature is provided.

         Changes
         The DATA RECORDS clause is allowed in UCS COBOL.

F.5.10. ALTER Statement
         Description
         The ALTER statement has been placed in the obsolete category. This means that this
         feature will be removed from future revisions of the standard and should not be used
         when writing new programs.

         The use of the ALTER statement in a program results in a program that can be difficult
         to understand and maintain.

         The ALTER statement provides no unique functionality since the GO TO DEPENDING
         statement serves the same purpose.

         Expected Impact on ASCII COBOL Programs
         Some problems could occur. A diagnostic flagging this as an obsolete feature is
         provided.

         Changes
         The ALTER statement is allowed in UCS COBOL.




7831 0455ΓÇô022                                                                              FΓÇô37
UCS COBOL and ASCII COBOL Differences




F.5.11. The Optional Use of a Procedure Name in a GO TO
        Statement
       Description
       The optional use of procedure-name-1 in the GO TO statement has been placed in the
       obsolete category. This means that this feature will be removed from future revisions
       of the standard and should not be used when writing new programs.

       This feature requires the use of the ALTER statement, which is an obsolete language
       feature. If procedure-name-1 is not specified in format 1 of the GO TO statement, then
       an ALTER statement referring to that GO TO statement must be executed prior to the
       execution of the GO TO statement.

       Expected Impact on ASCII COBOL Programs
       A diagnostic flagging this as an obsolete feature is provided.

       Changes
       This feature is allowed in UCS COBOL.

F.5.12. REVERSED Phrase of the OPEN Statement
       Description
       The REVERSED phrase of the OPEN statement has been placed in the obsolete
       category. This means that this feature will be removed from future revisions of the
       standard and should not be used when writing new programs.

       Hardware is not widely available. Implementation was optional and the feature is
       infrequently used.

       Expected Impact on ASCII COBOL Programs
       A diagnostic flagging this as an obsolete feature is provided.

       Changes
       The REVERSED phrase of the OPEN statement is allowed in UCS COBOL.

F.5.13. STOP Literal Statement
       Description
       The literal variation of the STOP statement has been placed in the obsolete category.
       This means that this feature will be removed from future revisions of the standard and
       should not be used when writing new programs.

       This removes functions defined by the implementor and enhances program portability.




FΓÇô38                                                                          7831 0455ΓÇô022
                                               UCS COBOL and ASCII COBOL Differences




         Expected Impact on ASCII COBOL Programs
         A diagnostic flagging this as an obsolete feature is provided.

         Changes
         The STOP literal statement is allowed in UCS COBOL.

F.5.14. Segmentation Module
         Description
         The Segmentation module has been placed in the obsolete category. This means that
         this feature will be removed from future revisions of the standard and should not be
         used when writing new programs.

         This function is best provided by the Linking System component of the Universal
         Compiling System.

         Expected Impact on ASCII COBOL Programs
         Some problems could occur. A diagnostic flagging this as an obsolete feature is
         provided.

         Changes
         The Segmentation module is allowed in UCS COBOL.

F.5.15. Debug Module
         Description
         The Debug module has been placed in the obsolete category. This means that this
         feature will be removed from future revisions of the standard and should not be used
         when writing new programs.

         This function is best provided by an interactive debug facility, such as the
         Programmers Advanced Debugging System (PADS), which does not require UCS
         COBOL source statements.

         Expected Impact on ASCII COBOL Programs
         UCS COBOL allows debug module syntax, but ignores it. A diagnostic flagging this as
         an obsolete feature is provided.

         Changes
         Use PADS to debug UCS COBOL source programs.

Appendix G
Compatibility, Restrictions, and
Operational Considerations

         The following subsections explain the software with which UCS COBOL level 12R1 is
         compatible. The restrictions and considerations that affect the operation of UCS
         COBOL are also explained.


G.1. Compatibility
         We recommend that you always use the D$WORK-WS keyword option when
         compiling UCOB programs that use DMS. This forces the DMS D$WORK data
         structure to be allocated in WORKING-STORAGE, even if the program places the
         DMCA into COMMON using the INVOKE clause. If the option is not used and the
         INVOKE places the DMCA into COMMON, D$WORK will be placed at the end of
         COMMON-STORAGE after all the user variables. If the layout of COMMON-STORAGE
         section is not identical in all programs units in an executable then the user variables
         can overlay the D$WORK data structure, and can result in execution failure.

         If your programs INVOKE the DMCA into COMMON and you want the D$WORK data
         structure to be allocated at the end of COMMON-STORAGE (the default), then do not
         use the D$WORK-WS keyword option. However, this is not recommended. Refer to
         Section 2.2.7, ΓÇ£Compiler Call Keyword Options for Program Control,ΓÇ¥ for a description
         of this keyword option.

G.1.1. Language Support System (LSS) Level
         You must install the Language Support System (LSS) level 14R1 to generate code for
         level 12R1 of the UCS COBOL compiler. Previous levels of LSS are not compatible with
         the current compiler. The following subsection describes other issues that can affect
         the compatibility of your existing UCS COBOL programs.

G.1.2. Compatibility with ASCII COBOL
         UCS COBOL is compatible with the ANSI COBOL Standard X3.23-1985. In general, UCS
         COBOL supports standard features of X3.23-1974 as well as standard feature
         extensions documented in the current ASCII COBOL Programming Reference
         Manual.




7831 0455ΓÇô022                                                                                 GΓÇô1
Compatibility, Restrictions, and Operational Considerations




        The ASCII COBOL Supplementary Reference Manual documents the ASCII COBOL
        features that UCS COBOL does not implement. The differences in implementation of
        the two systems and the ASCII COBOL features that were not carried forward into
        UCS COBOL affect the compatibility between ASCII COBOL and UCS COBOL. UCS
        COBOL contains several compiler keyword options that reduce the incompatibilities
        due to implementation and standard differences.

G.1.3. Compatibility with Previous Versions of UCOB
        GOBACK is now a new COBOL verb. Any use of the word GOBACK, either as a data
        name or a procedure name, will no longer be allowed in a UCS COBOL program. Any
        use of a data name or procedure name of GOBACK will need to be changed.

        ADDRESS, NULL, and NULLS are now unreserved words. An incompatibility was
        introduced if a user had a data name declared as ADDRESS and used that data name
        as a sender or receiver in a SET statement. A similar incompatibility was also
        introduced for data names NULL or NULLS used as sending item in a SET statement or
        in a conditional statement (i.e. an IF statement). In those situations, NULL and NULLS
        are now treated as a two-word value of binary zeroes. Any use of the data names
        ADDRESS, NULL or NULLS within SET or relational statements will need to be
        changed.


G.2. Operational Considerations
        Operational considerations are permanent and are provided to promote the effective
        use of a software product.

        The following operational considerations apply to UCS COBOL:

        ∩é╖   You must use the SDDL processor with the appropriate options to produce an
            object module S$WORK. If you use the SDDL to create a relocatable S$WORK,
            you cannot use the S$WORK in the same run unit with UCS object modules.
        ∩é╖   The UCS COBOL compiler now performs all the functions of the ASCII COBOL
            Data Manipulation Language Preprocessor (ADMLP). Therefore, do not use the
            source output from the ADMLP processor as input to the UCS COBOL compiler.
            If you try to use source output from the ADMLP processor as input to UCS
            COBOL and execute the resulting object module, an incorrect entry point into
            DMS 2200 occurs and the execution fails.
        ∩é╖   When you compile a DMS program with UCOB, it is recommended that you
            always compile it with the D$WORK-WS keyword option. This keyword option
            ensures that the DMS D$WORK data structure is always allocated in WORKING-
            STORAGE section. Refer to the discussion at the beginning of this appendix and
            the explanation for the keyword option in section 2.2.7, ΓÇ£Compiler Call Keyword
            Options for Program Control.ΓÇ¥
        ∩é╖   Checkpoint Restart (CKRS) will not work for a program that contains calls to
            I18NLIB (either implicit or explicit) because I18NLIB is a subsystem that cannot be
            restarted with the current design of CKRS. To avoid the problem, remove any
            explicit calls to I18NLIB routines from the source program and use the keyword
            option NO-I18N-IO to eliminate any implicit calls to the I18NLIB.



GΓÇô2                                                                              7831 0455ΓÇô022
                          Compatibility, Restrictions, and Operational Considerations




         UCS compiler implementations are different from basic mode compilers in several
         ways:
         ∩é╖   UCS compiler output is in the object module format; it is not in relocatable binary
             (RB) format.
         ∩é╖   Data allocation uses a byte-aligned algorithm.
         ∩é╖   User calling sequences follow different rules for parameter passing and for code
             and data referencing.
         ∩é╖   The library supporting UCS is different from the libraries used by the basic mode
             compilers.
         ∩é╖   The product LSS generates the code for the UCS compilers and is separately
             installed. The version of LSS installed on your system must be compatible with
             the language front ends (for example, UC, UCOB, and UFTN).
